title.zh: 卷一百 列傳第三十八: 孟鑄 宗端脩 完顏閭山 路鐸 完顏伯嘉 朮虎筠壽 張煒 高竑 李復亨
title.en: Volume 100 Biographies 38: Meng Zhu, Zong Duanxiu, Wan Yanlushan, Lu Duo, Wan Yanbojia, Pai Huyunshou, Zhang Wei, Gao Hong, Li Fuheng
title.raw: 卷一百 列傳第三十八: 孟鑄 宗端脩 完顏閭山 路鐸 完顏伯嘉 朮虎筠壽 張煒 高竑 李復亨 Volume 100 Biographies 38: Meng Zhu, Zong Duanxiu, Wan Yanlushan, Lu Duo, Wan Yanbojia, Pai Huyunshou, Zhang Wei, Gao Hong, Li Fuheng

sentences.zh: 孟鑄，大定末，補尚書省令史。

translations.literal: Meng Zhu, at the end of the Dading era, was appointed a clerk in the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Meng Zhu entered service late in the Dading reign as a clerk in the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 明昌元年，御史台奏薦戶部員外郎李獻可、完顏掃合、太府丞徒單繹、宮籍監丞張庸、右警巡使袞、禮部主事蒲察振壽、戶部主事郭蛻、應奉翰林文字移刺益、中都鹽鐵判官趙皓、尚書省令史劉昂及鑄十一人皆剛正可用。

translations.literal: In the first year of Mingchang, the Censorate memorialized recommending the Vice Director of the Ministry of Revenue Li Xiank, Wan Yan Saohe, Grand Treasury Vice Director Tushi Dan Yi, Palace Registry Supervisor Zhang Yong, Right Patrol Commissioner Gun, Ministry of Rites Clerk Pucha Zhenshou, Ministry of Revenue Clerk Guo Tui, Hanlin Attendant Yila Yi, Central Capital Salt and Iron Commissioner Zhao Hao, Secretariat Clerk Liu Ang, and Zhu—eleven men in all—as upright and fit for use.
translations.idiomatic: In Mingchang 1 (1190), the Censorate recommended eleven men as upright and capable: Li Xiank, vice director of the Ministry of Revenue; Wanyan Saohe; Tushi Dan Yi, vice director of the Grand Treasury; Zhang Yong, supervisor of the palace registry; Gun, right patrol commissioner; Pucha Zhenshou and Guo Tui, clerks of the Ministries of Rites and Revenue; Yila Yi, Hanlin attendant; Zhao Hao, salt and iron commissioner of the central capital; Liu Ang, a Secretariat clerk; and Meng Zhu himself.

sentences.zh: 詔除獻可右司諫，掃合磁州刺史，繹秘書丞，庸中都右警巡使，袞彰國軍節度副使，振壽治書侍御史，蛻同知定武軍節度使事，益翰林修撰，皓都水丞，昂戶部主事，鑄刑部主事。

translations.literal: An edict appointed Xiank Right Office Remonstrator, Saohe prefect of Cizhou, Yi Secretariat Director, Yong Right Patrol Commissioner of the Central Capital, Gun military commissioner vice commissioner of Zhangguo Army, Zhenshou supervising secretary of the Secretariat, Tui associate commissioner of Dingwu Army, Yi Hanlin reviser, Hao Director of Waterways, Ang Revenue Clerk, and Zhu Ministry of Punishments Clerk.
translations.idiomatic: The throne then appointed them: Xiank as right remonstrator of the Secretariat; Saohe prefect of Cizhou; Yi as director of the Secretariat archive; Yong as right patrol commissioner of the capital; Gun as deputy military commissioner of the Zhangguo army; Zhenshou as supervising secretary; Tui as associate commissioner of the Dingwu army; Yi as Hanlin reviser; Hao as director of waterways; Ang as a revenue clerk; and Zhu as a clerk in the Ministry of Punishments.

sentences.zh: 累遷中都路按察副使、南京副留守、河平軍節度使。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to Surveillance Vice Commissioner of the Central Capital Circuit, Deputy Military Commissioner of Nanjing, and Military Commissioner of the Heping Army.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through the posts of surveillance vice commissioner on the Central Capital circuit, deputy military commissioner at Nanjing, and military commissioner of the Heping army.

sentences.zh: 泰和四年，入為御史中丞，召見於香閣。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Taihe, he entered the capital as Censor-in-Chief and was summoned to audience in the Fragrant Pavilion.
translations.idiomatic: In Taihe 4 (1204) he was recalled to serve as censor-in-chief and received in audience at the Fragrant Pavilion.

sentences.zh: 上謂鑄曰：「朕自知卿，非因人薦舉也。

translations.literal: The emperor said to Zhu: "I know you myself; it was not because others recommended you.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor told him, "I chose you myself—I did not rely on anyone else's recommendation.

sentences.zh: 御史責任甚重，往者台官乃推求細故，彈劾小官，至於巨室重事，則畏徇不言。

translations.literal: The censors' responsibility is very weighty. In the past, officials of the bureau would pursue petty matters and impeach minor officials, but when it came to great houses and weighty affairs, they feared and kept silent.
translations.idiomatic: The censorate carries grave responsibility. Former bureau officials hunted out trifles and impeached petty officers, yet when powerful families and serious matters were involved they shrank back and said nothing.

sentences.zh: 其勤乃職，無廢朕命。」

translations.literal: You should diligently perform your duties and not neglect my command."
translations.idiomatic: Apply yourself to your office and do not fail my charge."

sentences.zh: 是歲，自春至夏，諸郡少雨。

translations.literal: That year, from spring through summer, the commanderies had little rain.
translations.idiomatic: That year rain was scarce across the commanderies from spring into summer.

sentences.zh: 鑄奏：「今歲愆陽，已近五月，比至得雨，恐失播種之期，可依種麻菜法，擇地形稍下處撥畦種穀，穿土作井，隨宜灌溉。」

translations.literal: Zhu memorialized: "This year the sun is out of season; it is already nearly the fifth month. By the time rain comes, I fear the sowing season will be lost. One may follow the method used for planting hemp and vegetables—choose slightly lower ground, set out furrows to plant grain, dig wells in the earth, and irrigate as appropriate."
translations.idiomatic: Zhu submitted: "The drought this year has already lasted into late spring. If we wait for rain we may miss the planting season. We could adopt the method used for hemp and vegetable plots—select lower ground, lay out beds for grain, sink wells, and irrigate where needed."

sentences.zh: 上從其言，區種法自此始。

translations.literal: The emperor followed his words, and the method of compartment planting began from this.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor accepted his advice, and compartment planting was introduced from that time.

sentences.zh: 無何，奏彈知大興府事紇石烈執中過惡，其文略曰：「京師百郡之首，四方取則。

translations.literal: Before long, he memorialized impeaching He Shilie Zhizhong, prefect of Daxing, for his transgressions. The text in summary said: "The capital is the head of the hundred commanderies; the four quarters take it as their model.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he impeached He Shilie Zhizhong, administrator of Daxing prefecture. His memorial in essence read: "The capital stands at the head of the empire's commanderies; all regions look to it as their standard.

sentences.zh: 知府執中貪殘專恣，不奉法令，自奉聖州罪解以後，怙罪不悛，蒙朝廷恩貸，轉生跋扈。

translations.literal: Prefect Zhizhong is greedy, cruel, and willfully arbitrary; he does not obey laws and orders. Since his punishment was lifted at Fengshengzhou, he has relied on his guilt without reform. Favored with the court's gracious pardon, he has grown ever more overbearing.
translations.idiomatic: Prefect Zhizhong is rapacious, brutal, and arbitrary, heedless of law. Since his sentence was remitted at Fengshengzhou he has clung to his offenses without reform; pardoned by the court, he has become only more domineering.

sentences.zh: 雄州詐奪人馬，平州冒支己俸，無故破魏廷碩家，發其塚墓。

translations.literal: At Xiongzhou he fraudulently seized others' horses; at Pingzhou he drew his own salary improperly; without cause he destroyed the household of Wei Tingshuo and opened his tomb.
translations.idiomatic: At Xiongzhou he seized people's horses by fraud; at Pingzhou he drew salary to which he was not entitled; without cause he ruined Wei Tingshuo's family and desecrated his grave.

sentences.zh: 拜表以調鷹不赴，祈雨聚妓戲嬉，毆詈同僚，擅令住職，失師帥之體。

translations.literal: He submitted a memorial citing hawk-training and did not attend; at a rain prayer he gathered courtesans for sport; he beat and reviled colleagues; he on his own authority ordered them to halt their duties—losing the bearing of a commander.
translations.idiomatic: He excused himself from court on the pretext of training hawks; at a rain ceremony he gathered entertainers for revelry; he assaulted and abused colleagues and on his own authority ordered them to suspend their duties—conduct unworthy of a metropolitan governor.

sentences.zh: 乞行黜退，以厭人望。」

translations.literal: I beg that he be dismissed and removed to satisfy public expectation."
translations.idiomatic: I ask that he be dismissed to satisfy the people's expectations."

sentences.zh: 上以執中東宮舊人，頗右之，謂鑄曰：「執中粗人，似有跋扈者。」

translations.literal: Because Zhizhong was an old associate of the Eastern Palace, the emperor favored him somewhat and said to Zhu: "Zhizhong is a rough man; there seems to be something overbearing about him."
translations.idiomatic: Zhizhong had been a companion in the heir apparent's household, and the emperor leaned in his favor. He told Zhu, "Zhizhong is a coarse fellow—there may be something overbearing in him."

sentences.zh: 鑄曰：「明天子在上，豈容有跋扈之臣？」

translations.literal: Zhu said: "With a bright Son of Heaven above, how could an overbearing minister be tolerated?"
translations.idiomatic: Zhu replied, "With a sage emperor on the throne, how could an overbearing minister be tolerated?"

sentences.zh: 上悟，詔尚書省問之。

translations.literal: The emperor understood and ordered the Secretariat to investigate him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor took his point and ordered the Secretariat to investigate.

sentences.zh: 泰和五年，唐、鄧、河南屢有警，議者謂宋且敗盟。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Taihe, Tang, Deng, and Henan repeatedly had alarms; discussants said Song was about to break the alliance.
translations.idiomatic: In Taihe 5 (1205) there were repeated alarms along the Tang, Deng, and Henan frontiers, and court opinion held that Song was preparing to break the treaty.

sentences.zh: 六年正月，宋賀正旦使陳克俊等朝辭，上使鑄就館諭克俊以國家涵容之意，果不詳此旨，恐兵未可息也。

translations.literal: In the first month of the sixth year, the Song envoys for New Year's congratulations Chen Kejun and others took leave of court. The emperor sent Zhu to the lodge to instruct Kejun in the state's spirit of forbearance: if they truly did not understand this intent, I fear arms might not yet cease.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of Taihe 6, when the Song New Year's envoys led by Chen Kejun were taking leave, the emperor sent Zhu to their lodge to convey the court's wish for forbearance—if Song failed to grasp that message, he warned, the fighting might not end.

sentences.zh: 使以上言達宋主。

translations.literal: The envoy reported upward so that the words reached the Song ruler.
translations.idiomatic: The envoy relayed the message to the Song emperor.

sentences.zh: 章宗本無意用兵，故再三諭之。

translations.literal: Zhangzong originally had no intention of using troops, and therefore repeatedly instructed them thus.
translations.idiomatic: Zhangzong had never wished for war and so repeated the admonition again and again.

sentences.zh: 鑄論提刑司改按察司，差官複察，權削望輕。

translations.literal: Zhu argued that when the Office of Punishment Investigation was changed to the Surveillance Office, dispatching officials for re-investigation diminished authority and prestige.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu argued that renaming the punishment investigation office as the surveillance office and sending separate officers to re-review cases had weakened its standing.

sentences.zh: 下尚書省議。

translations.literal: The matter was sent down to the Secretariat for deliberation.
translations.idiomatic: The proposal was referred to the Secretariat for discussion.

sentences.zh: 參知政事賈鉉奏：「乞差監察時，即別遣官偕往，更不復察，諸疑獄並令按察司從正與決，庶幾可慰人望。」

translations.literal: Vice Director of the Secretariat Jia Xian memorialized: "When surveillance officers are dispatched, let separate officials be sent along with them but no longer conduct re-investigation; let all doubtful cases be decided outright by the Surveillance Office—then perhaps public expectation may be satisfied."
translations.idiomatic: Vice director Jia Xian proposed: "When surveillance officers are sent out, another official should accompany them, but there should be no second review; doubtful cases should be decided on the spot by the surveillance office—that should restore public confidence."

sentences.zh: 從之。

translations.literal: This was followed.
translations.idiomatic: The court approved his proposal.

sentences.zh: 永豐庫官不守宿，因而被盜，上召登聞鼓院官欲有所問，皆不在。

translations.literal: An official of the Yongfeng treasury did not keep night watch, and as a result it was robbed. The emperor summoned officials of the Petition Drum Court intending to question them, but none were present.
translations.idiomatic: Treasury officers at Yongfeng failed to keep night watch, and the depot was robbed. When the emperor summoned officials of the petition drum court to question them, none were on duty.

sentences.zh: 上諭鑄曰：「此輩慢法如此，御史台所職何事也！」

translations.literal: The emperor instructed Zhu: "These men treat the law with such contempt—what is the Censorate's office for!"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor told Zhu, "They treat the law with such contempt—what is the censorate for?"

sentences.zh: 複諭御史大夫宗肅及鑄曰：「朕聞唐宰相宿省中，卿等所知也。

translations.literal: He again instructed Censor-in-Chief Zong Su and Zhu: "I have heard that Tang chancellors lodged overnight in the Secretariat—you know this as well.
translations.idiomatic: He also told censor-in-chief Zong Su and Zhu, "I have heard that Tang chancellors slept overnight in the Secretariat—you know that tradition.

sentences.zh: 台官、六部官、其餘司局亦嘗宿直。

translations.literal: Censorate officials, Six Ministries officials, and other bureaus also once kept night duty.
translations.idiomatic: Censorate officers, Six Ministries staff, and other agencies once kept night watches as well.

sentences.zh: 今尚書省左右司官宿直，餘亦當准此。」

translations.literal: Now the Left and Right Offices of the Secretariat keep night duty; the rest should also follow this standard."
translations.idiomatic: The left and right offices of the Secretariat now keep night duty; the rest of you should follow the same rule."

sentences.zh: 八年，除絳陽軍節度使。

translations.literal: In the eighth year he was appointed Military Commissioner of the Jiangyang Army.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year of his service he was made military commissioner of the Jiangyang army.

sentences.zh: 至甯元年，複為御史中丞。

translations.literal: In the first year of Zhining, he again became Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhining 1 (1213) he was again appointed censor-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 紇石烈執中作亂，召鑄及右諫議大夫張行信俱至大興府，問曰：「汝輩向來彈我者耶？」

translations.literal: When He Shilie Zhizhong rebelled, he summoned Zhu and Right Remonstrator Zhang Xingxin together to Daxing prefecture and asked: "Were you the ones who impeached me before?"
translations.idiomatic: When He Shilie Zhizhong rose in rebellion, he summoned Zhu and right remonstrator Zhang Xingxin to Daxing and asked, "Were you the ones who impeached me before?"

sentences.zh: 鑄等各以正言答之。

translations.literal: Zhu and the others each answered with upright words.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu and the others answered him forthrightly.

sentences.zh: 執中乃遣還家，曰：「且須後命。」

translations.literal: Zhizhong then sent them back home, saying: "Wait for further orders."
translations.idiomatic: Zhizhong sent them home, saying, "Await further orders."

sentences.zh: 既而執中死，鑄亦尋卒。

translations.literal: Before long Zhizhong died, and Zhu also soon passed away.
translations.idiomatic: Zhizhong was killed soon afterward, and Zhu died not long after.

sentences.zh: 宗端修

translations.literal: Zong Duanxiu
translations.idiomatic: Zong Duanxiu

sentences.zh: 宗端修，字平叔，汝州人。

translations.literal: Zong Duanxiu, style name Pingshu, was a man of Ruzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Zong Duanxiu, whose style was Pingshu, came from Ruzhou.

sentences.zh: 章宗避睿宗諱上一字，凡太祖諸子皆加「山」為「崇」，改「宗」氏為「姬」氏。

translations.literal: Zhangzong avoided the taboo on the preceding character of Ruizong's name: all sons of Taizu had "shan" changed to "chong," and the surname "Zong" was changed to "Ji."
translations.idiomatic: To avoid the taboo on Emperor Ruizong's personal name, Zhangzong ordered the character shan changed to chong in the names of all Taizu's sons and the clan name Zong changed to Ji.

sentences.zh: 端修好學，喜名節，中大定二十二年進士第。

translations.literal: Duanxiu loved learning and prized reputation and integrity; he passed the jinshi examination in the twenty-second year of Dading.
translations.idiomatic: Duanxiu was studious and cared deeply for honor; he passed the jinshi examination in Dading 22 (1182).

sentences.zh: 明昌間，補尚書省令史。

translations.literal: During Mingchang he was appointed a Secretariat clerk.
translations.idiomatic: During the Mingchang era he became a clerk in the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 承安元年，監察御史孫椿年、武簡職事不修舉，詔以端修及範鐸代之。

translations.literal: In the first year of Cheng'an, Surveillance Censors Sun Chunnian and Wu Jian did not diligently perform their duties; an edict appointed Duanxiu and Fan Duo to replace them.
translations.idiomatic: In Cheng'an 1 (1196), surveillance censors Sun Chunnian and Wu Jian were found negligent in office, and Duanxiu and Fan Duo were ordered to replace them.

sentences.zh: 是時元妃李氏兄弟干預朝政，端修上書乞遠小人。

translations.literal: At that time the brothers of the Yuan consort surnamed Li interfered in court politics; Duanxiu submitted a memorial begging to keep petty men at a distance.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the brothers of Consort Yuan, Lady Li, were meddling in government, and Duanxiu memorialized asking that petty men be kept at a distance.

sentences.zh: 上遣李喜兒傳詔部端修：「小人為誰，其以姓名對。」

translations.literal: The emperor sent Li Xi'er to transmit an edict questioning Duanxiu: "Who are the petty men? Answer with their names."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent Li Xi'er to question him: "Who are these petty men? Give their names."

sentences.zh: 端修對曰：「小人者，李仁惠兄弟。」

translations.literal: Duanxiu answered: "The petty men are the brothers Li Renhui."
translations.idiomatic: Duanxiu answered, "The petty men are the brothers Li Renhui."

sentences.zh: 仁惠，喜兒賜名也。

translations.literal: Renhui was the name bestowed on Xi'er.
translations.idiomatic: Renhui was the name the throne had bestowed on Xi'er.

sentences.zh: 喜兒不敢隱，具奏之。

translations.literal: Xi'er did not dare conceal it and reported everything in full.
translations.idiomatic: Xi'er did not dare conceal the charge and reported it in full to the emperor.

sentences.zh: 上雖責喜兒兄弟，而不能去也。

translations.literal: Although the emperor reproached Xi'er and his brothers, he could not remove them.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor rebuked Xi'er and his brothers but could not dismiss them.

sentences.zh: 四年，複上書言事，宰相惡之，坐以不經台官直進奏帖，准上書不以實，削一官，期年後敘。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he again submitted a memorial on affairs of state. The chancellors hated him and convicted him on the grounds of not going through censorate officials but directly submitting a memorial, applying the statute on memorials not based in fact—his rank was reduced by one step, with reinstatement after one year.
translations.idiomatic: Four years later he memorialized again on state affairs. The chancellors took offense and punished him for bypassing the censorate with a direct memorial, invoking the statute against unsubstantiated petitions—he was demoted one rank, with reinstatement after a year.

sentences.zh: 章宗知端修不為眾所容，釋之，改大理司直。

translations.literal: Zhangzong knew Duanxiu was not tolerated by the multitude and released him, changing his post to Director of the Court of Judicial Review.
translations.idiomatic: Zhangzong knew Duanxiu was unpopular at court and pardoned him, appointing him a director in the Court of Judicial Review.

sentences.zh: 泰和四年，遷大理丞，召見於香閣。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Taihe he was transferred to Vice Director of the Court of Judicial Review and summoned to audience in the Fragrant Pavilion.
translations.idiomatic: In Taihe 4 he was promoted to vice director of the Court of Judicial Review and received in audience at the Fragrant Pavilion.

sentences.zh: 上謂端修曰：「汝前為御史，以幹能見用。

translations.literal: The emperor said to Duanxiu: "When you were previously a censor, you were employed for your capability.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor told him, "When you served as a censor I valued your ability.

sentences.zh: 汝言多細碎，不究其實，嘗令問汝，亦不汝罪。

translations.literal: Your words were often petty and trivial and did not investigate the facts. I once had you questioned but did not punish you.
translations.idiomatic: Your charges were often petty and not grounded in fact. I had you questioned once but did not punish you.

sentences.zh: 及為大理司直，乃能稱職，用是擢汝為丞，盡乃心力，惟法是守，勿問上位宰執所見何如，汝其志之！」

translations.literal: When you became a director of the Court of Judicial Review, you were able to fulfill your duties; therefore I promote you to vice director. Exhaust your mind and strength, uphold only the law, and do not ask what the high ministers above think—keep this in mind!"
translations.idiomatic: As a judicial director you proved yourself fit for office, and so I promote you to vice director. Give your full effort, uphold the law alone, and pay no heed to what the chancellors above may think—remember that!"

sentences.zh: 知大同府紇石烈執中陳言，下大理寺議。

translations.literal: He Shilie Zhizhong, administrator of Datong prefecture, submitted a statement; the matter was sent down to the Court of Judicial Review for deliberation.
translations.idiomatic: He Shilie Zhizhong, administrator of Datong, submitted a petition, and the case was referred to the Court of Judicial Review.

sentences.zh: 端修謂執中言事涉私治罪。

translations.literal: Duanxiu held that Zhizhong's statement involved private interests and should be punished.
translations.idiomatic: Duanxiu ruled that Zhizhong's petition involved private interests and warranted punishment.

sentences.zh: 詔以端修別出情見不當，與司直溫敦按帶各削一官解職。

translations.literal: An edict held that Duanxiu's separate presentation of the facts of the case was improper; he and Director Wendantuo Andai each had one rank reduced and were dismissed from office.
translations.idiomatic: An edict found Duanxiu's separate opinion improper; he and director Wendantuo Andai were each demoted one rank and dismissed.

sentences.zh: 久之，為節度副使，卒官。

translations.literal: After a long while he became a military commissioner vice commissioner and died in office.
translations.idiomatic: After some time he was made a deputy military commissioner and died in that post.

sentences.zh: 端修終以直道不振于時，自守愈篤。

translations.literal: Duanxiu in the end, because the upright way did not flourish in his time, guarded himself all the more steadfastly.
translations.idiomatic: Because integrity found little reward in his day, Duanxiu held all the more firmly to his principles.

sentences.zh: 妻死不復更娶，獨居二十年，士論高之。

translations.literal: After his wife died he did not marry again, living alone for twenty years; scholars esteemed him highly.
translations.idiomatic: After his wife's death he never remarried and lived alone for twenty years, winning high praise among scholars.

sentences.zh: 汝州司候遊彥哲將之官，問為政。

translations.literal: You Yanjie, judicial assistant of Ruzhou, was about to take up his post and asked about governing.
translations.idiomatic: You Yanjie, a judicial assistant of Ruzhou, was about to take up his post and asked Duanxiu how to govern.

sentences.zh: 端修曰：「為政不難，治氣養心而已。」

translations.literal: Duanxiu said: "Governing is not difficult—it is only regulating the breath and nourishing the mind."
translations.idiomatic: Duanxiu said, "Governing is not difficult—it is simply regulating your breath and cultivating your mind."

sentences.zh: 彥哲不達，端修曰：「心正則不私，氣平則不暴。

translations.literal: Yanjie did not understand; Duanxiu said: "When the mind is upright there is no selfishness; when the breath is level there is no violence.
translations.idiomatic: Yanjie did not understand, so Duanxiu explained: "When the mind is upright you will not be partial; when your temper is calm you will not be harsh.

sentences.zh: 為政之術，盡於此矣。」

translations.literal: The art of governing is fully contained in this."
translations.idiomatic: The whole art of governing lies in that alone."

sentences.zh: 完顏閭山

translations.literal: Wanyan Lushan
translations.idiomatic: Wanyan Lushan

sentences.zh: 路鐸，字宣叔，伯達子也。

translations.literal: Lu Duo, style name Xuanshu, was the son of Lu Boda.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Duo, styled Xuanshu, was the son of Lu Boda.

sentences.zh: 明昌三年，為左三部司正。

translations.literal: In the third year of Mingchang he was Director of the Left Three Departments.
translations.idiomatic: In Mingchang 3 (1192) he served as director of the left three departments.

sentences.zh: 上書言事，召見便殿，遷右拾遣。

translations.literal: He submitted a memorial on affairs of state, was summoned to audience in the side hall, and was transferred to Right Supplementation Censor.
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized on state affairs, was received in the side hall, and was promoted to right supplementation censor.

sentences.zh: 明年，盧溝河決，鐸請自玄同口以下、丁村以上無修舊堤，縱使分流，以殺減水勢。

translations.literal: The next year the Lugou River burst its banks; Duo requested that from below Xuankou down to above Dingcun the old dikes not be repaired, allowing the water to divide and flow so as to reduce its force.
translations.idiomatic: The following year the Lugou River broke its banks. Duo proposed leaving the old dikes unrepaired from Xuankou downstream to Dingcun upstream, allowing the flood to spread and thereby lessen its force.

sentences.zh: 詔工部尚書胥持國與鐸同檢視。

translations.literal: An edict ordered Minister of Works Xu Chiguo and Duo to inspect together.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered minister of works Xu Chiguo and Duo to inspect the works together.

sentences.zh: 章宗將幸景明宮，是歲民饑，不可行。

translations.literal: Zhangzong was about to visit Jingming Palace; that year the people were famine-stricken, and the journey could not be made.
translations.idiomatic: Zhangzong planned to visit Jingming Palace, but famine that year made the journey impossible.

sentences.zh: 御史中丞董師中上書諫，鐸與左補闕許安仁繼之，賜對禦閣。

translations.literal: Censor-in-Chief Dong Shizhong submitted a memorial remonstrating; Duo and Left Supplementation Censor Xu Anren followed, and they were granted audience in the Imperial Pavilion.
translations.idiomatic: Censor-in-chief Dong Shizhong remonstrated by memorial; Duo and left supplementation censor Xu Anren joined him, and all three were granted audience in the imperial pavilion.

sentences.zh: 詔尚書省曰：「朕不禁暑熱，欲往山后。

translations.literal: An edict to the Secretariat said: "I do not fear summer heat and wish to go to the mountains behind.
translations.idiomatic: An edict to the Secretariat read: "I do not shrink from the summer heat and wished to go to the northern hills.

sentences.zh: 今台諫言民間多闕食，朕初不盡知，既已知之，其忍自奉以重困民哉。」

translations.literal: Now the censors and remonstrators say that among the people many lack food. At first I did not fully know this; now that I know, how could I indulge myself and add to the people's distress?"
translations.idiomatic: The censors now report widespread hunger among the people. I did not fully understand this before, but now that I do, how could I indulge myself and add to their hardship?"

sentences.zh: 乃罷行。

translations.literal: The journey was then canceled.
translations.idiomatic: The journey was canceled.

sentences.zh: 尚書左丞完顏守貞每論政事，守正不移，與同列不合，罷知東平府事，台諫因而擠之。

translations.literal: Left Vice Director of the Secretariat Wanyan Shouzhen, whenever he discussed government affairs, held to the upright without wavering; he did not agree with his colleagues and was dismissed to administer Dongping prefecture, and the censors and remonstrators thereupon squeezed him out.
translations.idiomatic: Left vice director Wanyan Shouzhen was steadfast in debate and clashed with his colleagues; he was dismissed to govern Dongping, and the censorate used the occasion to force him out.

sentences.zh: 鐸上書論守貞賢，可複用，其言太切，召對於崇政殿。

translations.literal: Duo submitted a memorial arguing that Shouzhen was worthy and could be reused; his words were too sharp, and he was summoned for audience in Chongzheng Hall.
translations.idiomatic: Duo memorialized that Shouzhen was worthy of recall; his language was so blunt that he was summoned to Chongzheng Hall.

sentences.zh: 既而章宗以鐸書語大臣，於是尚書左丞烏林答願、參知政事夾穀衡、胥持國奏路鐸以梁冀比右丞相，所言狂妄，不稱諫職。

translations.literal: Then Zhangzong reported Duo's memorial to the great ministers; thereupon Left Vice Director Wulindada Yuan, Vice Director Jiagu Heng, and Xu Chiguo memorialized that Lu Duo had compared the right chancellor to Liang Ji, that his words were reckless, and that they did not suit the remonstrator's office.
translations.idiomatic: Zhangzong then showed Duo's memorial to the senior ministers. Left vice director Wulindada Yuan, vice director Jiagu Heng, and Xu Chiguo reported that Duo had likened the right chancellor to the Han tyrant Liang Ji—language so reckless it was unworthy of a remonstrator.

sentences.zh: 右丞相，夾谷清臣也。

translations.literal: The right chancellor was Jiagu Qingchen.
translations.idiomatic: The right chancellor was Jiagu Qingchen.

sentences.zh: 上曰：「周昌以傑、紂比漢高祖，高祖不以為忤。

translations.literal: The emperor said: "Zhou Chang compared Jie and Zhou to Emperor Gaozu of Han, and Gaozu did not take it as an offense.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "Zhou Chang compared Jie and Zhou to Emperor Gaozu of Han, and Gaozu took no offense.

sentences.zh: 路鐸以梁冀比丞相耳。」

translations.literal: Lu Duo only compared Liang Ji to the chancellor."
translations.idiomatic: Lu Duo only compared Liang Ji to a chancellor."

sentences.zh: 頃之，守貞入為平章政事。

translations.literal: Before long Shouzhen entered the capital as Grand Councilor.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward Shouzhen was recalled as grand councilor.

sentences.zh: 五年，複與禮部尚書張暐、御史中丞董師中、右諫議大夫賈守謙、翰林修撰完顏撒刺諫幸景明宮，語多激切，章宗不能堪，遣近侍局直長李仁願召凡諫北幸者詣尚書省，詔曰：「卿等諫北幸甚善，但其間頗失君臣之體耳。」

translations.literal: In the fifth year he again joined Minister of Rites Zhang Wei, Censor-in-Chief Dong Shizhong, Right Remonstrator Jia Shouqian, and Hanlin Reviser Wanyan Saci in remonstrating against visiting Jingming Palace; their words were mostly sharp and cutting. Zhangzong could not bear it and sent Chief of the Inner Service Bureau Li Renyuan to summon all who had remonstrated against the northern journey to the Secretariat, with an edict saying: "Your remonstrance against the northern journey was very good, but in it you rather lost the proper form between ruler and minister."
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year he again joined minister of rites Zhang Wei, censor-in-chief Dong Shizhong, right remonstrator Jia Shouqian, and Hanlin reviser Wanyan Saci in opposing the visit to Jingming Palace. Their language was so sharp that Zhangzong could not bear it. He sent Li Renyuan of the inner service bureau to summon all who had remonstrated to the Secretariat with this message: "Your advice against the northern journey was excellent, but you rather overstepped the bounds between ruler and minister."

sentences.zh: 是歲，郝忠愈獄起，事密，諫官不能察其詳，議者頗謂事涉鎬王永中，思有以寬解上意。

translations.literal: That year the case of Hao Zhongyu arose; the matter was secret, and remonstrating officials could not discern its details. Discussants largely said the affair involved Prince Yong of Hao and sought some way to ease the emperor's mind.
translations.idiomatic: That year the Hao Zhongyu case broke—a secret affair whose details the remonstrators could not learn. Many believed it implicated Prince Yong of Hao and sought some way to soften the emperor's resolve.

sentences.zh: 右諫議大夫賈守謙上封事，鐸繼之，尤切直。

translations.literal: Right Remonstrator Jia Shouqian submitted a sealed memorial; Duo followed, especially sharp and direct.
translations.idiomatic: Right remonstrator Jia Shouqian submitted a sealed memorial, and Duo followed with an even blunter one.

sentences.zh: 上優容之，謂鐸曰：「汝言諸王皆有覬心，遊其門者不無橫議，是何言也。

translations.literal: The emperor treated them with forbearance and said to Duo: "You say all the princes harbor ambitious designs and that those who frequent their gates do not lack reckless talk—what kind of words are these?
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was indulgent and said to Duo, "You say every prince harbors ambition and that visitors to their households spread reckless talk—what sort of language is that?

sentences.zh: 但朕不罪諫官耳。」

translations.literal: But I do not punish remonstrating officials."
translations.idiomatic: Still, I do not punish remonstrators."

sentences.zh: 頃之，尚書省奏擬鐸同知河北西路轉運使事，詔再任右拾遺，謂宰相曰：「鐸敢言，但識短耳。

translations.literal: Before long the Secretariat memorialized proposing Duo as Associate Commissioner of the Hebei West Circuit Transport Office; an edict reappointed him Right Supplementation Censor, and the emperor told the chancellors: "Duo dares to speak, but his judgment is short.
translations.idiomatic: Soon the Secretariat proposed appointing Duo associate transport commissioner of the Hebei West circuit, but an edict kept him as right supplementation censor. The emperor told the chancellors, "Duo is bold in speech, but his judgment is shallow.

sentences.zh: 朕嘗詰責而氣不沮。」

translations.literal: I once reproached and questioned him, yet his spirit was not daunted."
translations.idiomatic: I have rebuked him, yet his spirit never flags."

sentences.zh: 鐸因召對，論宰相權太重。

translations.literal: Duo, because of a summoned audience, argued that the chancellors' power was too heavy.
translations.idiomatic: At a later audience Duo argued that the chancellors held too much power.

sentences.zh: 上曰：「凡事由朕，宰相安得權重。」

translations.literal: The emperor said: "In all affairs it is I who decide—how could the chancellors have heavy power?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "All affairs rest with me—how could the chancellors be overpowerful?"

sentences.zh: 既而複奏曰：「乞陛下勿泄此言，泄則臣齏粉矣。」

translations.literal: Then he again memorialized: "I beg Your Majesty not to leak these words; if leaked, your servant will be ground to powder."
translations.idiomatic: Duo then added, "I beg Your Majesty not to repeat what I have said—if you do, I shall be destroyed."

sentences.zh: 上曰：「宰相安能齏粉人！」

translations.literal: The emperor said: "How could chancellors grind people to powder!"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor replied, "Chancellors cannot destroy a man!"

sentences.zh: 至是，章宗並以此言告宰相，雖留再任，宰相愈銜之。

translations.literal: At this point Zhangzong also reported these words to the chancellors; although Duo was kept for reappointment, the chancellors bore an ever deeper grudge against him.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Zhangzong repeated Duo's warning to the chancellors anyway. Though Duo was kept in office, they resented him all the more.

sentences.zh: 改右補闕。

translations.literal: He was changed to Right Supplementation Censor.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to right supplementation censor.

sentences.zh: 自完顏守貞再入相，以政事為己任，胥持國方幸，尤忌守貞，並忌鐸輩。

translations.literal: From the time Wanyan Shouzhen again entered the chancellery and took government affairs as his own charge, Xu Chiguo was then in favor and especially resented Shouzhen, and likewise resented Duo and his fellows.
translations.idiomatic: After Wanyan Shouzhen returned to the chancellery and took charge of policy, Xu Chiguo—then in favor at court—resented him especially and bore equal ill will toward Duo and his colleagues.

sentences.zh: 鐸輩雖嘗為守貞論辨而不相附。

translations.literal: Although Duo and his fellows had once argued on Shouzhen's behalf, they did not attach themselves to him.
translations.idiomatic: Though Duo and his fellows had once spoken up for Shouzhen, they did not align themselves with him.

sentences.zh: 鐸論邊防，守貞以為掇拾唐人餘論，皆不行。

translations.literal: When Duo discussed border defense, Shouzhen regarded it as picking up leftover Tang discussions, and none of it was implemented.
translations.idiomatic: When Duo proposed border reforms, Shouzhen dismissed them as recycled Tang platitudes, and none were adopted.

sentences.zh: 及守貞持鎬王永中事久不決，鐸等亦上言切諫，並指以為黨。

translations.literal: When Shouzhen held the affair of Prince Yong of Hao Wang Yongzhong unresolved for long, Duo and others also submitted sharp remonstrances, and all were pointed out as a faction.
translations.idiomatic: As Shouzhen prolonged the case of Prince Yong of Hao, Duo and others remonstrated sharply as well, and all were denounced as a clique.

sentences.zh: 上乃出守貞知濟南府，凡曾薦守貞者皆黜降，謂宰臣曰：「董師中謂台省無守貞不可治，路鐸、李敬義皆稱舉之者。

translations.literal: The emperor then sent Shouzhen out to administer Jinan prefecture; all who had recommended Shouzhen were demoted or reduced in rank. He told the chancellors: "Dong Shizhong said the censorate and Secretariat could not be governed without Shouzhen; Lu Duo and Li Jingyi were among those who praised and recommended him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor dismissed Shouzhen to govern Jinan and demoted everyone who had recommended him. He told the chancellors, "Dong Shizhong said the censorate could not function without Shouzhen; Lu Duo and Li Jingyi were among his champions.

sentences.zh: 然三人者後俱可用，今姑出之。」

translations.literal: Yet these three men may all be used later; for now let them be sent out."
translations.idiomatic: All three may yet prove useful; for now I am merely sending them out."

sentences.zh: 上複曰：「路鐸敢言，甚有時名，一旦外補，人將謂朕不能容直臣。

translations.literal: The emperor again said: "Lu Duo dares to speak and has considerable contemporary reputation; if he is suddenly sent out to a provincial post, people will say I cannot tolerate upright ministers.
translations.idiomatic: He added, "Lu Duo is outspoken and widely admired. If I send him to the provinces, people will say I cannot tolerate honest ministers.

sentences.zh: 可選敢言及才識處鐸右者。」

translations.literal: One may select someone bold in speech and in talent and judgment superior to Duo."
translations.idiomatic: Find someone as bold and more capable than Duo."

sentences.zh: 參知政事馬琪奏曰：「鐸雖知無不言，然亦多不當理。」

translations.literal: Vice Director Ma Qi memorialized: "Although Duo knows there is nothing he does not speak of, much of it is also not reasonable."
translations.idiomatic: Vice director Ma Qi said, "Duo speaks without restraint, but much of what he says is unreasonable."

sentences.zh: 上曰：「諫官非但取敢言，亦須間有出朕意表者，乃有裨益耳。」

translations.literal: The emperor said: "Remonstrating officials are valued not only for daring to speak; there must also occasionally be words that go beyond what I expect—only then is there benefit."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor replied, "Remonstrators must do more than speak boldly—they must sometimes surprise me, or they are of no use."

sentences.zh: 於是，吏部尚書董師中出為陝西路轉運使，鐸為南京留守判官。

translations.literal: Thereupon Minister of Personnel Dong Shizhong was sent out as Transport Commissioner of the Shaanxi Circuit, and Duo became Administrative Aide to the Military Commissioner of Nanjing.
translations.idiomatic: Dong Shizhong was sent out as transport commissioner of the Shaanxi circuit, and Duo became administrative aide to the Nanjing military commissioner.

sentences.zh: 戶部郎中李敬義方使高麗還，即出為安化軍節度副使。

translations.literal: Revenue Bureau Director Li Jingyi had just returned from an embassy to Goryeo and was immediately sent out as Deputy Military Commissioner of the Anhua Army.
translations.idiomatic: Li Jingyi of the revenue bureau, just returned from an embassy to Goryeo, was immediately made deputy military commissioner of the Anhua army.

sentences.zh: 詔曰：「卿等昨來交薦守貞公正可用，今坐所舉失實耳。」

translations.literal: An edict said: "You recently jointly recommended Shouzhen as upright and usable; now you are punished because your recommendation did not match the facts."
translations.idiomatic: An edict read: "You jointly recommended Shouzhen as upright and capable; you are punished only because that recommendation proved false."

sentences.zh: 承安二年，召為翰林修撰，同看讀陳言文字。

translations.literal: In the second year of Cheng'an he was summoned as Hanlin Reviser, jointly reviewing submitted memorials and statements.
translations.idiomatic: In Cheng'an 2 he was recalled as Hanlin reviser and assigned to review submitted memorials.

sentences.zh: 上召禮部尚書張暐、大理卿麻安上及鐸，問趙晏所言十事，因問董師中、張萬公優劣。

translations.literal: The emperor summoned Minister of Rites Zhang Wei, Chief Justice Ma Anshang, and Duo, asking about the ten matters spoken of by Zhao Yan, and then asking the relative merits of Dong Shizhong and Zhang Wangong.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor summoned Zhang Wei, Ma Anshang, and Duo to discuss Zhao Yan's ten proposals and to ask their view of Dong Shizhong versus Zhang Wangong.

sentences.zh: 鐸奏：「師中附胥持國以進，趙樞、張複亨、張嘉貞皆出持國門下，嘉貞複趨走襄之門。

translations.literal: Duo memorialized: "Shizhong relied on Xu Chiguo to advance; Zhao Shu, Zhang Fuheng, and Zhang Jiazhen all came from Chiguo's school, and Jiazhen again rushed to attend on Xiang.
translations.idiomatic: Duo reported that Shizhong had risen through Xu Chiguo's patronage, that Zhao Shu, Zhang Fuheng, and Zhang Jiazhen were all Chiguo's protégés, and that Jiazhen now curried favor with Xiang as well.

sentences.zh: 持國不可複用，若再相，必亂綱紀。」

translations.literal: Chiguo cannot be reused; if made chancellor again, he will surely disorder the statutes and regulations."
translations.idiomatic: Chiguo must not be restored; if he becomes chancellor again he will surely wreck the government."

sentences.zh: 上曰：「朕豈複相此人，但遷官二階使致仕，何為不可？」

translations.literal: The emperor said: "How could I make this man chancellor again? Only to promote him two ranks and let him retire—why not?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "I would never make him chancellor again—only promote him two ranks and let him retire. What harm is there in that?"

sentences.zh: 持國党聞之，怒愈甚。

translations.literal: Chiguo's faction heard this and grew angrier still.
translations.idiomatic: Chiguo's faction heard of it and grew only more enraged.

sentences.zh: 改監察御史。

translations.literal: He was changed to Surveillance Censor.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to surveillance censor.

sentences.zh: 參知政事楊伯通引用鄉人李浩，鐸劾奏：「伯通以公器結私恩，左司郎中賈益、知除武鬱承望風旨，不詳檢起複條例。」

translations.literal: Vice Director Yang Botong employed his fellow townsman Li Hao; Duo impeached and memorialized: "Botong uses public office to form private favor; Left Office Director Jia Yi and Appointment Officer Wu Yu followed the wind of his intent without carefully examining the regulations on reinstatement."
translations.idiomatic: Vice director Yang Botong had appointed a fellow townsman, Li Hao. Duo impeached him: "Botong trades public office for private favor; Jia Yi and appointment officer Wu Yu followed his lead without checking the rules on reinstatement."

sentences.zh: 涉妄冒，大夫張暐抑之不行。

translations.literal: It involved reckless presumption; Censor-in-Chief Zhang Wei suppressed it and it was not carried out.
translations.idiomatic: The case involved improper appointment; censor-in-chief Zhang Wei blocked it.

sentences.zh: 上命同知大興府事賈鉉詰問。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered Associate Administrator of Daxing Jia Xian to question and investigate.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered Jia Xian, associate administrator of Daxing, to investigate.

sentences.zh: 張暐、伯通待罪於家。

translations.literal: Zhang Wei and Botong awaited punishment at home.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Wei and Botong awaited judgment at home.

sentences.zh: 賈鉉奏：「近詔書詰問御史大夫張暐。

translations.literal: Jia Xian memorialized: "Recently an edict questioned Censor-in-Chief Zhang Wei.
translations.idiomatic: Jia Xian reported: "A recent edict questioned censor-in-chief Zhang Wei.

sentences.zh: 暐言路鐸嘗稟會楊伯通私用鄉人李浩。

translations.literal: Wei said that Lu Duo had once reported that Yang Botong privately employed his fellow townsman Li Hao.
translations.idiomatic: Wei said Lu Duo had reported Yang Botong's private appointment of Li Hao.

sentences.zh: 暐以為彈絀大臣，須有阿曲實跡，恐所劾不當，台綱愈壞，令再體察。

translations.literal: Wei held that in impeaching great ministers there must be bent favor and solid traces of fact; he feared the impeachment was improper and the censorate's standards would be further damaged, and ordered further investigation.
translations.idiomatic: Wei held that impeaching a senior minister required solid proof of favoritism; fearing the charge might fail and damage the censorate, he ordered a further review.

sentences.zh: 賈益言除授皆宰執公議，奏稟，不見伯通私任形跡。」

translations.literal: Jia Yi said all appointments and dismissals were matters of public deliberation among the chancellors, reported upward for approval, and no trace of Botong's private appointment was seen."
translations.idiomatic: Jia Yi said all appointments were decided by the chancellors in open council and reported upward; he saw no sign of a private appointment by Botong."

sentences.zh: 於是，詔責鐸言事輕率，慰諭伯通治事如故。

translations.literal: Thereupon an edict reproached Duo for speaking rashly on affairs and comforted and instructed Botong to govern as before.
translations.idiomatic: An edict rebuked Duo for rash speech and told Botong to resume his duties.

sentences.zh: 頃之，遷侍御史，主奏事。

translations.literal: Before long he was transferred to Attending Censor, in charge of memorials.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was promoted to attending censor and placed in charge of memorials.

sentences.zh: 監察御史姬端修以言事下吏，使御史台令史郭公仲達意于大夫張暐及鐸。

translations.literal: Surveillance Censor Ji Duanxiu was handed over to the law officers for speaking on affairs; he had the Censorate clerk Guo Gongzhong convey his intent to Censor-in-Chief Zhang Wei and Duo.
translations.idiomatic: Surveillance censor Ji Duanxiu was arrested for his memorial; he had censorate clerk Guo Gongzhong sound out Zhang Wei and Duo beforehand.

sentences.zh: 暐與鐸奏事殿上，上問：「姬端修彈事嘗申台官否？」

translations.literal: Wei and Duo reported affairs in the hall; the emperor asked: "When Ji Duanxiu impeached, did he ever report to censorate officials?"
translations.idiomatic: When Zhang Wei and Duo reported at court, the emperor asked whether Ji Duanxiu had consulted the censorate before impeaching.

sentences.zh: 對曰：「嘗來面議。」

translations.literal: They answered: "He once came to discuss in person."
translations.idiomatic: They answered that he had come to discuss it in person.

sentences.zh: 端修款伏乃雲：「只曾與侍禦私議，大夫不知也。」

translations.literal: Duanxiu confessed fully and then said: "I only privately discussed with the attending censor; the censor-in-chief did not know."
translations.idiomatic: Duanxiu confessed: "I discussed it only with the attending censor; the censor-in-chief knew nothing."

sentences.zh: 既而端修杖七十收贖，公仲杖七十替罷。

translations.literal: Then Duanxiu was beaten seventy strokes and allowed to redeem; Gongzhong was beaten seventy strokes and dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: Duanxiu received seventy strokes and paid a fine; Gongzhong received seventy strokes and was dismissed.

sentences.zh: 暐、鐸坐奏事不實，暐追一官，鐸兩官，皆解職。

translations.literal: Wei and Duo were convicted of reporting affairs untruthfully; Wei had one rank reduced, Duo two ranks, and both were dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Wei and Duo were punished for false reporting; Wei lost one rank, Duo two, and both were dismissed.

sentences.zh: 頃之，起為泰定軍節度副使。

translations.literal: Before long he was reappointed Deputy Military Commissioner of the Taiding Army.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon reappointed deputy military commissioner of the Taiding army.

sentences.zh: 上謂宰臣曰：「凡言事者，議及朕躬亦無妨，語涉宰相，間有憎嫌，何以得進？」

translations.literal: The emperor told the chancellors: "For all who speak on affairs, it is no harm if they discuss even my person; but when words touch the chancellors, there is occasionally personal hatred—how can they advance?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor told the chancellors, "Let remonstrators criticize even me—but when their words touch the chancellors, personal grudges block their advancement. How can that continue?"

sentences.zh: 詔左司計鐸資考至正五品，即除東平府治中。

translations.literal: An edict ordered the Left Office to calculate Duo's seniority as reaching the fifth rank of the positive series, and he was immediately appointed Administrative Director of Dongping prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered his seniority calculated to the fifth positive rank and appointed him administrative director of Dongping.

sentences.zh: 未幾，景州闕刺史，尚書省已奏郭歧為之，詔特改鐸為景州刺史，仍勿送審官院。

translations.literal: Before long Jingzhou lacked a prefect; the Secretariat had already memorialized Guo Qi for the post, but an edict specially changed it to Duo as Prefect of Jingzhou, and still did not send it to the Review Office.
translations.idiomatic: When Jingzhou needed a prefect the Secretariat had already nominated Guo Qi, but an edict appointed Duo instead and waived review by the appointments office.

sentences.zh: 鐸述十二訓以教民。

translations.literal: Duo set forth twelve admonitions to instruct the people.
translations.idiomatic: Duo composed twelve admonitions to instruct the people.

sentences.zh: 詔曰：「路鐸十二訓皆勸人為善，遍諭州郡使知之。」

translations.literal: An edict said: "Lu Duo's twelve admonitions all exhort people to do good; let them be proclaimed throughout the commanderies so all may know them."
translations.idiomatic: An edict declared: "Lu Duo's twelve admonitions all exhort people to virtue—proclaim them in every commandery."

sentences.zh: 遷陝西路按察副使。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Surveillance Vice Commissioner of the Shaanxi Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to surveillance vice commissioner of the Shaanxi circuit.

sentences.zh: 坐以糾彈之官與京兆府治中蒲察張鐵、總管判官辛孝儉、推官愛剌宴飲，奪路一官解職。

translations.literal: He was convicted because, as an impeaching official, he feasted with Administrative Director of Jingzhao Pucha Zhang Tie, Administrative Aide of the Military Commissioner Xin Xiaojian, and Investigating Officer Aila; Duo's road rank was reduced by one step and he was dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: He was dismissed and demoted one rank for feasting with Jingzhao director Pucha Zhang Tie, military commissioner aide Xin Xiaojian, and investigating officer Aila—conduct unbecoming an impeaching officer.

sentences.zh: 泰和六年，召為翰林待制兼知登聞鼓院，累除孟州防禦使。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Taihe he was summoned as Hanlin Attendant-in-Waiting and concurrently Administrator of the Petition Drum Court; he was repeatedly promoted to Defender of Mengzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In Taihe 6 he was recalled as Hanlin attendant-in-waiting and administrator of the petition drum court, and eventually made defender of Mengzhou.

sentences.zh: 貞祐初，城破，投沁水死。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Zhenyou, when the city fell, he threw himself into the Qin River and died.
translations.idiomatic: When the city fell early in Zhenyou, he drowned himself in the Qin River.

sentences.zh: 鐸剛正，曆官台諫，有直臣之風。

translations.literal: Duo was upright and firm; having served in the censorate and remonstrance offices, he had the bearing of an upright minister.
translations.idiomatic: Duo was upright and firm; through years in the censorate and remonstrance offices he embodied the spirit of an honest minister.

sentences.zh: 為文尚奇，詩篇溫潤精緻，號《虛舟居士集》雲。

translations.literal: In writing he favored the unusual; his poems were warm, refined, and delicate. His collected works were titled Collected Works of the Empty Boat Recluse.
translations.idiomatic: His prose favored the striking; his poetry was warm and finely wrought. His collected works were titled Collected Works of the Empty Boat Recluse.

sentences.zh: 完顏伯嘉

translations.literal: Wanyan Bojia
translations.idiomatic: Wanyan Bojia

sentences.zh: 完顏伯嘉字，輔之，北京路訛魯古必剌猛安人。

translations.literal: Wanyan Bojia, style name Fuzhi, was a man of the Yilugu Bila military colony on the Northern Capital circuit.
translations.idiomatic: Wanyan Bojia, styled Fuzhi, came from the Yilugu Bila colony on the Northern Capital circuit.

sentences.zh: 明昌二年進士，調中都左警巡判官。

translations.literal: A jinshi of the second year of Mingchang, he was assigned as Left Patrol Commissioner of the Central Capital.
translations.idiomatic: A jinshi of Mingchang 2, he was posted as left patrol commissioner of the central capital.

sentences.zh: 孝懿皇后妹晉國夫人家奴買漆不酬直，伯嘉鉤致晉國用事奴數人系獄。

translations.literal: A slave of the Lady of Jin state, younger sister of Empress Xiaoyi, bought lacquer and did not pay the price; Bojia investigated and had several of the Lady of Jin's powerful slaves imprisoned.
translations.idiomatic: When a slave of the Lady of Jin—sister of Empress Xiaoyi—bought lacquer without paying, Bojia arrested several of her powerful household slaves.

sentences.zh: 晉國白章宗，章宗曰：「姨酬其價，則奴釋矣。」

translations.literal: The Lady of Jin reported to Zhangzong; Zhangzong said: "If my aunt pays the price, the slaves will be released."
translations.idiomatic: The Lady of Jin appealed to Zhangzong, who said, "If my aunt pays the price, release the slaves."

sentences.zh: 由是豪右屏跡。

translations.literal: From this the powerful local families withdrew and kept out of sight.
translations.idiomatic: After that the local magnates kept their distance.

sentences.zh: 改寶坻丞。

translations.literal: He was changed to Vice Magistrate of Baodi.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to vice magistrate of Baodi.

sentences.zh: 補尚書省令史，除太學助教、監察御史。

translations.literal: He was appointed a Secretariat clerk and then made Assistant Instructor of the Imperial Academy and Surveillance Censor.
translations.idiomatic: He became a Secretariat clerk, then assistant instructor of the Imperial Academy and surveillance censor.

sentences.zh: 劾奏平章政事僕散揆。

translations.literal: He impeached and memorialized against Grand Councilor Pusan Kui.
translations.idiomatic: He impeached grand councilor Pusan Kui.

sentences.zh: 或曰：「與宰相有隙，奈何？」

translations.literal: Someone said: "You have a rift with the chancellor—what then?"
translations.idiomatic: Someone warned him, "You have a feud with the chancellor—what then?"

sentences.zh: 伯嘉曰：「職分如此。」

translations.literal: Bojia said: "Such is the duty of the office."
translations.idiomatic: Bojia replied, "That is my duty."

sentences.zh: 遷平涼治中。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Administrative Director of Pingliang.
translations.idiomatic: He was made administrative director of Pingliang.

sentences.zh: 累官莒州刺史。

translations.literal: He rose through offices to Prefect of Juzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He eventually rose to prefect of Juzhou.

sentences.zh: 讞屬縣盜，伯嘉曰：「饑寒為盜，得錢二千，經月不使一錢雲何？

translations.literal: In a case of theft in a subordinate county, Bojia said: "Stealing from hunger and cold—having gotten two thousand cash, how could he go a month without spending a single coin?
translations.idiomatic: In a theft case from a subordinate county he said, "A man driven to theft by hunger might steal two thousand cash—but how could he go a month without spending a single coin?

sentences.zh: 此必官兵捕他盜不獲，誣以准罪耳。」

translations.literal: This must be that government troops failed to catch another thief and falsely charged this one to meet the quota."
translations.idiomatic: Soldiers must have failed to catch another thief and framed this man to meet their quota."

sentences.zh: 詰之，果然。

translations.literal: He questioned them, and it was indeed so.
translations.idiomatic: He questioned them, and it proved true.

sentences.zh: 詔與按察官俱推排物力，召見於香閣。

translations.literal: An edict ordered him together with surveillance officials to assess property and wealth; he was summoned to audience in the Fragrant Pavilion.
translations.idiomatic: He was ordered to assess property valuations with surveillance officials and received in audience at the Fragrant Pavilion.

sentences.zh: 大安中，三遷同知西京留守，權本路安撫使。

translations.literal: During Da'an he was thrice promoted to Associate Military Commissioner of the Western Capital and acted as Pacification Commissioner of that circuit.
translations.idiomatic: During the Da'an era he was thrice promoted to associate military commissioner of the Western Capital and served as acting pacification commissioner of the circuit.

sentences.zh: 貞祐初，遷順義軍節度使。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Zhenyou he was transferred to Military Commissioner of the Shunyi Army.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Zhenyou he was made military commissioner of the Shunyi army.

sentences.zh: 居父母喪，卒哭，起複震武軍節度使兼宣撫副使，提控太和嶺諸隘。

translations.literal: While in mourning for his parents, at the end of the wailing period he was recalled to serve as Military Commissioner of the Zhenwu Army and Pacification Vice Commissioner, controlling the passes of Taihe Ridge.
translations.idiomatic: While mourning his parents he was recalled at the end of the mourning period as military commissioner of the Zhenwu army and pacification vice commissioner, charged with the passes of Taihe Ridge.

sentences.zh: 副統李鵬飛誣殺彰國軍節度使牙改，詔伯嘉治之。

translations.literal: Deputy Commander Li Pengfei falsely killed Military Commissioner Yagai of the Zhangguo Army; an edict ordered Bojia to try the case.
translations.idiomatic: Deputy commander Li Pengfei had falsely killed Zhangguo military commissioner Yagai; Bojia was ordered to investigate.

sentences.zh: 貞祐四年三月，伯嘉奏：「西京副統程琢智勇過人，持心忠孝，以私財募集壯士二萬，複取渾源、白登，有恢復山西之志，已命駐於弘州矣。

translations.literal: In the third month of the fourth year of Zhenyou, Bojia memorialized: "Western Capital Deputy Commander Cheng Zhuo surpasses others in wisdom and courage and holds loyalty and filial piety in his heart. With private wealth he recruited twenty thousand stalwarts, recovered Hunyuan and Baideng, and has the will to restore Shanxi; he has already been ordered to garrison at Hongzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of Zhenyou 4, Bojia memorialized: "Deputy commander Cheng Zhuo of the Western Capital is exceptionally brave and loyal. With his own funds he raised twenty thousand men, retook Hunyuan and Baideng, and aims to recover Shanxi. He has been ordered to garrison at Hongzhou.

sentences.zh: 近者靖大中、完顏毛吉打以三千人歸國，各遷節度副使。

translations.literal: Recently Jing Dazhong and Wanyan Maojida returned to the state with three thousand men; each was promoted to military commissioner vice commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Recently Jing Dazhong and Wanyan Maojida returned with three thousand men and were each promoted to deputy military commissioner.

sentences.zh: 今山西已不守，琢收合餘眾，盡忠於國，百戰不挫。

translations.literal: Now Shanxi is no longer held; Zhuo gathers the remaining troops, is wholly loyal to the state, and though he fights a hundred battles is not broken.
translations.idiomatic: Shanxi is lost, yet Zhuo has rallied the remnants, served the state with full loyalty, and fought on undefeated through countless battles.

sentences.zh: 臣恐失機會，輒擬琢昭勇大將軍，同知西京留守事，兼領一路義軍，給以空名敕二十道，許擇有謀略者充州縣。」

translations.literal: Your servant fears losing the opportunity and ventures to propose Zhuo as General of Manifest Courage, Associate Military Commissioner of the Western Capital, concurrently leading the volunteer army of one circuit, granted twenty blank commission documents, and permitted to select men of strategy to fill prefectures and counties."
translations.idiomatic: I fear we may miss our chance and propose appointing Zhuo general of manifest courage and associate military commissioner of the Western Capital, with command of the circuit's volunteer forces, twenty blank commissions, and authority to appoint capable men to prefectural and county posts."

sentences.zh: 制可，仍賜琢姓夾穀氏。

translations.literal: The proposal was approved, and Zhuo was moreover granted the surname Jiagu.
translations.idiomatic: The proposal was approved, and Zhuo was granted the surname Jiagu.

sentences.zh: 琢請曰：「前代皆賜國姓，不系他族，如蒙更賜，榮莫大焉。」

translations.literal: Zhuo requested: "Former dynasties all bestowed the imperial surname, not tying one to another clan; if I might receive it again, the glory would be beyond measure."
translations.idiomatic: Zhuo requested the imperial surname itself, saying that no honor could be greater.

sentences.zh: 詔更賜完顏氏。

translations.literal: An edict then bestowed the surname Wanyan.
translations.idiomatic: An edict granted him the surname Wanyan.

sentences.zh: 是月，伯嘉遷元帥左監軍，知太原府事，河東北路宣撫使。

translations.literal: That month Bojia was transferred to Left Army Supervisor of the Marshal, Administrator of Taiyuan prefecture, and Pacification Commissioner of the Hedong North Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: That month Bojia was made left army supervisor of the marshal, administrator of Taiyuan, and pacification commissioner of the Hedong North circuit.

sentences.zh: 以同知太原府斡勒合打為彰國軍節度使、宣撫副使。

translations.literal: Associate Administrator of Taiyuan Wolie Hedai was made Military Commissioner of the Zhangguo Army and Pacification Vice Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Wolie Hedai, associate administrator of Taiyuan, was made military commissioner of the Zhangguo army and pacification vice commissioner.

sentences.zh: 六月，斡勒合打奏：「同知西京留守完顏琢恃與宣撫使伯嘉雅善，徙居代州，肆為侵掠。

translations.literal: In the sixth month Wolie Hedai memorialized: "Associate Military Commissioner of the Western Capital Wanyan Zhuo relies on his close friendship with Pacification Commissioner Bojia, has moved to Daizhou, and rampages in plunder.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month Hedai reported that Zhuo, relying on his friendship with Bojia, had moved to Daizhou and was plundering the countryside.

sentences.zh: 遙授太原治中，權堅州刺史完顏斜烈私離邊面，臣白伯嘉，伯嘉不悅，遣臣護送糧運於代州。

translations.literal: Remotely appointed Administrative Director of Taiyuan and Acting Prefect of Jianzhou Wanyan Xielie privately left the frontier; your servant informed Bojia, and Bojia was displeased and sent your servant to escort grain transport to Daizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Xielie, remotely appointed Taiyuan director and acting Jianzhou prefect, had left his post without permission. When I reported this to Bojia he was displeased and sent me to escort grain convoys to Daizhou instead.

sentences.zh: 臣請益兵，乃以羸卒數百見付，半無鎧仗。

translations.literal: Your servant requested additional troops but was given only several hundred weak soldiers, half without armor and weapons.
translations.idiomatic: I asked for reinforcements but received only a few hundred weak troops, half without armor.

sentences.zh: 臣複為言，伯嘉怒臣，榜掠幾死。

translations.literal: When your servant spoke again, Bojia was angry with your servant and beat him with the cudgel nearly to death.
translations.idiomatic: When I protested again, Bojia had me beaten nearly to death.

sentences.zh: 臣立功累年，頗有寸效，伯嘉挾私陵轢，無複宣撫同僚之禮。

translations.literal: Your servant has rendered merit for many years and has had some small effect; Bojia, holding private grudges, oppresses and shows no longer the courtesy due between pacification colleagues.
translations.idiomatic: I have served with merit for years, yet Bojia abuses his authority from private spite and treats a fellow pacification commissioner with contempt.

sentences.zh: 臣欲不言，恐他日反為所誣，無以自明。」

translations.literal: Your servant wished not to speak, but feared that another day he might instead be slandered by him and have no means to clear himself."
translations.idiomatic: I would have kept silent, but I feared he would slander me later and I would have no defense."

sentences.zh: 上問宰臣，奏曰：「太原重鎮，防秋在邇，請敕諭和解。」

translations.literal: The emperor questioned the chancellors; they memorialized: "Taiyuan is a vital stronghold and autumn defense is near; we beg an edict instructing them to reconcile."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor consulted the chancellors, who urged an edict ordering reconciliation before the autumn campaign at vital Taiyuan.

sentences.zh: 詔曰：「太原兵沖，若以私忿廢國事，國家何賴焉！

translations.literal: An edict said: "Taiyuan is militarily critical; if because of private resentment you abandon state affairs, on whom can the state rely!
translations.idiomatic: An edict declared: "Taiyuan is strategically critical. If private quarrels derail state business, what can the dynasty rely on?

sentences.zh: 卿等同心戮力，以分北顧之憂，無執前非，誤大計也。」

translations.literal: You must join hearts and combine strength to share the worry of looking north; do not cling to past wrongs and mistake the great plan."
translations.idiomatic: Work together and share the burden of defending the north. Do not cling to old grievances and ruin the larger plan."

sentences.zh: 七月，伯嘉改知歸德府事，合打改武甯軍節度使。

translations.literal: In the seventh month Bojia was changed to Administrator of Guide prefecture, and Hedai was changed to Military Commissioner of the Wuning Army.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month Bojia was transferred to Guide prefecture and Hedai to the Wuning army.

sentences.zh: 御史台奏：「宣撫副使合打訴元帥伯嘉以私忿加箠楚，令本台廉問，既得其事，遂不復窮治。

translations.literal: The Censorate memorialized: "Pacification Vice Commissioner Hedai accused Marshal Bojia of beating him with the cudgel from private resentment; the bureau was ordered to investigate with integrity, and having obtained the facts, did not pursue it further.
translations.idiomatic: The censorate reported that Hedai had accused Bojia of beating him from private spite; after investigation confirmed the facts, no further action was taken.

sentences.zh: 若合打奏實，伯嘉安得無罪，伯嘉無罪，合打合坐欺罔，乞審正是非，明示黜陟。」

translations.literal: If Hedai's memorial is true, how can Bojia be without guilt? If Bojia is without guilt, Hedai should be convicted of deception; we beg to examine and establish right and wrong and clearly show demotion and promotion."
translations.idiomatic: If Hedai's charge is true, Bojia is guilty; if not, Hedai has deceived the throne. We ask that right and wrong be determined and appropriate rewards and punishments made clear."

sentences.zh: 宣宗曰：「今正防秋，且已。」

translations.literal: Xuanzong said: "Now is precisely the autumn defense—let it rest for now."
translations.idiomatic: Xuanzong said, "Autumn defense is upon us—let the matter drop for now."

sentences.zh: 初，河東行省胥鼎奏：「完顏伯嘉屢言同知西京留守兼台州刺史完顏琢，可倚之以複山西，朝廷遷官賜姓，令屯代北，扼太和嶺。

translations.literal: Earlier, Hedong Branch Secretariat Xu Ding memorialized: "Wanyan Bojia repeatedly said that Associate Military Commissioner of the Western Capital and Acting Prefect of Taizhou Wanyan Zhuo could be relied on to recover Shanxi; the court promoted him and bestowed a surname, ordering him to garrison north of Dai and hold Taihe Ridge.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Xu Ding of the Hedong branch secretariat had reported that Bojia repeatedly praised Zhuo as the man to recover Shanxi; the court had promoted him, granted him a surname, and ordered him to hold Taihe Ridge north of Dai.

sentences.zh: 今聞諸隘悉無琢兵，蓋琢挈太原之眾，保五台剽掠耳。

translations.literal: Now it is heard that at all the passes there are none of Zhuo's troops; probably Zhuo has taken the masses of Taiyuan, held Wutai, and is plundering—that is all.
translations.idiomatic: Now we hear his troops hold none of the passes; Zhuo has simply taken the Taiyuan forces, entrenched at Wutai, and turned to plunder.

sentences.zh: 如尚以伯嘉之言為可信，乞遣琢出太原，或徙之內地，分處其眾，以備不測之變。」

translations.literal: If Bojia's words are still trusted, I beg that Zhuo be sent out of Taiyuan or moved to the interior, his forces dispersed and stationed separately, to guard against unforeseen change."
translations.idiomatic: If Bojia's assurances are still believed, I ask that Zhuo be removed from Taiyuan or transferred inland and his forces dispersed to forestall unforeseen trouble."

sentences.zh: 宰臣奏：「已遣官體究琢軍，且令太原元帥府烏古論德升召琢使之矣。

translations.literal: The chancellors memorialized: "We have already dispatched officials to investigate Zhuo's army on the spot, and ordered the Taiyuan Marshal's headquarters under Wugulun Desheng to summon Zhuo and make him come.
translations.idiomatic: The chancellors replied that officials had been sent to investigate Zhuo's forces and that Wugulun Desheng of the Taiyuan marshal's headquarters had been ordered to summon him.

sentences.zh: 當以此意報鼎。」

translations.literal: This intent should be reported to Ding."
translations.idiomatic: This response should be relayed to Xu Ding.

sentences.zh: 無何，德升奏：「琢兵數萬分屯代州諸險，拒戰甚力，其眾烏合，非琢不可制。」

translations.literal: Before long Desheng memorialized: "Zhuo's troops number in the tens of thousands, garrisoned at the various passes of Daizhou; they resist battle with great force. His masses are a motley gathering—without Zhuo they cannot be controlled."
translations.idiomatic: Soon Desheng reported that Zhuo's tens of thousands held the Daizhou passes and fought fiercely; his motley force could be controlled only by Zhuo himself.

sentences.zh: 胥鼎複奏：「宣差提控古裏甲石倫言，琢方招降人，謀複山西，盤桓於忻、代、定、襄間，恣為侵擾，無複行意。

translations.literal: Xu Ding again memorialized: "Commissioned Controller Guli Jiashilun says Zhuo is now recruiting surrendered men, plotting to recover Shanxi, lingering between Xin, Dai, Ding, and Xiang, and wantonly making raids and disturbances, with no further intent to march.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Ding reported again that commissioner Guli Jiashilun said Zhuo was recruiting defectors, plotting to recover Shanxi, lingering between Xin, Dai, Ding, and Xiang, raiding at will, with no intention of advancing.

sentences.zh: 發掘民粟，並且。

translations.literal: He digs up the people's grain stores and consumes them as well.
translations.idiomatic: He seizes the people's grain stores and devours the supplies.

sentences.zh: 戕殺無辜，雖曰不煩官廩，博易為名，實則攘劫，欺國害民無如琢者。

translations.literal: He kills the innocent; though he says he does not trouble the official granaries, under the name of trade he actually plunders and robs—none deceives the state and harms the people like Zhuo.
translations.idiomatic: He slaughters innocents; though he claims not to burden the state granaries, his trade is mere plunder. No one deceives the state and harms the people like Zhuo.

sentences.zh: 石倫之言如此，臣已令帥府禁止之矣。」

translations.literal: Shilun's words are thus; your servant has already ordered the marshal's headquarters to forbid it."
translations.idiomatic: Such is Shilun's report; I have already ordered the marshal's headquarters to restrain him.

sentences.zh: 宰臣奏：「所遣官自忻、代來，雲不見劫掠之跡，惟如德升言便。」

translations.literal: The chancellors memorialized: "The dispatched officials coming from Xin and Dai say they do not see traces of plundering; only Desheng's words should be followed."
translations.idiomatic: The chancellors reported that officials returning from Xin and Dai had seen no sign of plunder and that Desheng's view should prevail.

sentences.zh: 從之。

translations.literal: This was followed.
translations.idiomatic: The court agreed.

sentences.zh: 伯嘉至歸德，上言，乞雜犯死罪以下納粟贖免。

translations.literal: Bojia arrived at Guide, submitted a memorial, and requested that for miscellaneous offenses below the death penalty, offenders be allowed to pay grain to redeem or exempt punishment.
translations.idiomatic: When Bojia reached Guide, he memorialized the throne, asking that for all miscellaneous crimes short of capital offense, offenders be permitted to pay grain in lieu of punishment.

sentences.zh: 宰臣奏：「伯嘉前在代州嘗行之，蓋一時之權，不可為常法。」

translations.literal: The chancellors memorialized: "Bojia had previously carried this out at Daizhou; it was only a temporary expedient and cannot be made a standing law."
translations.idiomatic: The chancellors replied: "Bojia tried this once at Daizhou—it was an emergency measure, not something that should become permanent law."

sentences.zh: 遂寢。

translations.literal: The proposal was thereupon shelved.
translations.idiomatic: And so the matter was dropped.

sentences.zh: 俄改簽樞密院事。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he was reassigned as a member of the Privy Council.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was appointed to the Privy Council.

sentences.zh: 未閱月，改知河南府事。

translations.literal: Before a month had passed, he was transferred to serve as prefect of Henan Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Less than a month later he was made prefect of Henan.

sentences.zh: 是時，甫經兵後，乏兵食，伯嘉令輸棗栗菜根足之，皆以為便。

translations.literal: At that time the region had just emerged from war and lacked military provisions; Bojia ordered that dates, chestnuts, and vegetable roots be submitted to make up the shortfall, and all regarded this as convenient.
translations.idiomatic: The province had just been ravaged by war and military rations were scarce. Bojia required that dates, chestnuts, and root vegetables be delivered to fill the gap—a measure everyone found practical.

sentences.zh: 興定元年，知河中府，充宣差都提控，未幾召為吏部尚書。

translations.literal: In the first year of Xingding he became prefect of Hezhong Prefecture and served as imperial commissioner and supreme military controller; before long he was summoned to be Minister of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Xingding he took up the prefecture of Hezhong as imperial commissioner and supreme military controller, and was soon recalled to serve as minister of personnel.

sentences.zh: 二年，改御史中丞。

translations.literal: In the second year he was transferred to Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he was made censor-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 初，貞祐四年十月，詔以兵部尚書、簽樞密院事蒲察阿裏不孫為右副元帥，備禦潼關、陝州。

translations.literal: Earlier, in the tenth month of the fourth year of Zhenyou, an edict appointed Pucha Aribusun, Minister of War and Privy Council member, as deputy commander-in-chief on the right to defend Tong Pass and Shaan Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Previously, in the tenth month of the fourth year of Zhenyou, an edict had named Pucha Aribusun—minister of war and Privy Council member—deputy commander-in-chief on the right, charged with the defense of Tong Pass and Shaan Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 次澠池土濠村，兵不戰而潰。

translations.literal: At Tuhhao Village near Mianchi, the army collapsed without fighting.
translations.idiomatic: Near Mianchi, at Tuhhao Village, the army broke and fled without ever giving battle.

sentences.zh: 阿裏不孫逸去，亡所佩虎符，變易姓名，匿柘城縣，與其妻妹前韓州刺史合喜男婦紇石烈氏及僕婢三人僦民舍居止。

translations.literal: Aribusun fled, lost the tiger tally he wore, changed his name, and hid in Zhecheng County, renting a commoner dwelling together with his wife younger sister—the former wife of He Xi, who had been prefect of Han Prefecture—a certain Lady Heshenilie—and three servants.
translations.idiomatic: Aribusun escaped, abandoning the tiger tally at his belt. He assumed a false name and went into hiding in Zhecheng County, where he rented a house together with his wife younger sister—Heshenilie, once the wife of the former Han prefect He Xi—and three servants.

sentences.zh: 合喜母徒單氏聞之，捕執紇石烈，斷其發，拘之佛寺中。

translations.literal: Hexi mother, Lady Tuhanshi, heard of this, seized Heshenilie, cut off her hair, and detained her in a Buddhist temple.
translations.idiomatic: When Hexi mother, Lady Tuhanshi, learned of it, she seized Heshenilie, sheared her hair, and held her prisoner in a Buddhist temple.

sentences.zh: 阿裏不孫複亡去。

translations.literal: Aribusun fled again.
translations.idiomatic: Aribusun fled once more.

sentences.zh: 監察御史完顏藥師劾奏：「乞就詰紇石烈及僕婢，當得所在。

translations.literal: Supervising Censor Wanyan Yaoshi submitted an impeachment: "I request that Heshenilie and the servants be interrogated at once—their whereabouts should thereby be obtained.
translations.idiomatic: Supervising Censor Wanyan Yaoshi impeached him, writing: "Interrogate Heshenilie and the servants without delay, and we shall learn where he is.

sentences.zh: 其妻子見在京師，亦無容不知，請窮治。」

translations.literal: His wife and children are now in the capital; they cannot but know. I request a thorough investigation."
translations.idiomatic: His wife and children are in the capital—they cannot fail to know. I beg that the matter be pursued to the end."

sentences.zh: 有司方系其家人，特命釋之，詔曰：「阿裏不孫若能自出，當免極罪。」

translations.literal: The authorities had just detained his family when a special order released them, with an edict stating: "If Aribusun can surrender himself, the gravest penalty shall be remitted."
translations.idiomatic: The authorities had just taken his family into custody when a special order set them free. An edict declared: "If Aribusun gives himself up, the death penalty will be waived."

sentences.zh: 阿裏不孫乃使其子上書，請圖後效。

translations.literal: Aribusun then had his son submit a memorial requesting to prove his merit through future service.
translations.idiomatic: Aribusun thereupon had his son submit a memorial asking leave to redeem himself through future deeds.

sentences.zh: 尚書省奏：「阿裏不孫幸特赦死，當詣闕自陳，乃令其子上書，猶懷顧望。」

translations.literal: The Ministry Secretariat memorialized: "Aribusun was fortunate to receive a special pardon from death; he ought to come to court and confess in person, yet he sends his son to submit a memorial, still hesitant and clinging to hope."
translations.idiomatic: The Secretariat reported: "Aribusun has been spared death by special grace. He should come to court and speak for himself. Instead he sends his son with a memorial—he still hangs back, hoping for more."

sentences.zh: 伯嘉劾之曰：「古之為將者，受命之日忘其家，臨陣之日忘其身，服喪衣、鑿凶門而出，以示必死。

translations.literal: Bojia impeached him, saying: "Ancient generals, upon receiving their commissions, forgot their families; upon entering battle, forgot their own bodies. They donned mourning garments, broke through the Gate of Ill Omen, and took the field to show they would surely die.
translations.idiomatic: Bojia pressed the charge: "The generals of old, on the day they received their orders, forgot their homes; on the day they entered battle, forgot their lives. They put on funeral dress, broke out through the Gate of Ill Omen, and marched forth to show they were ready to die.

sentences.zh: 進不求名，退不避罪，惟民是保。

translations.literal: They sought no fame in advancing and shunned no punishment in retreat; they had only the protection of the people in mind.
translations.idiomatic: They did not pursue glory when they advanced, nor shrink from blame when they withdrew—they cared for nothing but the welfare of the people.

sentences.zh: 阿裏不孫膺國重寄，握兵數萬，未陣而潰，委棄虎符，既不得援枹鼓以死敵，又不能負斧鑕而請罪，逃命竄伏，猥居裏巷，挾匿婦人，為此醜行。

translations.literal: Aribusun bore the state great trust, commanded tens of thousands of troops, yet collapsed before battle was joined, abandoned his tiger tally, could neither grasp drum and mace to die fighting the enemy nor carry axe and shackles to plead guilty, fled for his life and hid in secret, basely dwelling in back alleys and keeping a woman concealed—such is this disgraceful conduct.
translations.idiomatic: Aribusun was entrusted with the nation weightiest charge and commanded tens of thousands of men. Before a line was formed his army scattered. He cast away his tiger tally. He could neither take up drum and mace to die against the enemy, nor bear axe and fetters to answer for his crime. He ran for his life and hid in the alleys, sheltering a woman in shameful secrecy—conduct as foul as this.

sentences.zh: 聖恩寬大，曲赦其死，自當奔走闕庭，皇恐待命。

translations.literal: Imperial grace is broad; having mercifully pardoned his death, he ought naturally to rush to the imperial court, trembling in awe to await orders.
translations.idiomatic: The Son of Heaven mercy is vast. Having been spared the ultimate penalty, he should have raced to the palace steps and waited in trembling submission.

sentences.zh: 安坐要君，略無忌憚，跡其情罪，實不容誅。

translations.literal: Instead he sits at ease and holds the sovereign to ransom, utterly without fear; considering the circumstances of his guilt, he truly deserves no leniency in execution.
translations.idiomatic: Instead he sits comfortably at home, treating the throne with contempt, utterly without fear. Weighing the facts of his crime, he scarcely merits even this reprieve.

sentences.zh: 此而不懲，朝綱廢矣。

translations.literal: If this goes unpunished, court discipline will be ruined.
translations.idiomatic: If such a man is not punished, the discipline of the court is finished.

sentences.zh: 乞屍諸市以戒為臣之不忠者！」

translations.literal: I beg that his corpse be displayed in the marketplace to warn those ministers who are disloyal!"
translations.idiomatic: I beg that his body be exposed in the market as a warning to every disloyal minister!"

sentences.zh: 宣宗曰：「中丞言是，業已赦之矣。」

translations.literal: Emperor Xuanzong said: "The Censor-in-Chief speaks rightly, but he has already been pardoned."
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xuanzong replied: "The censor-in-chief is correct—but the pardon has already been granted."

sentences.zh: 阿裏不孫乃除名。
