translations.literal: Aribusun was then struck from the rolls.
translations.idiomatic: Aribusun was thereupon stripped of rank and office.

sentences.zh: 五月，充宣差河南提控捕蝗，許決四品以下。

translations.literal: In the fifth month he was appointed imperial commissioner for locust control in Henan, with authority to pass judgment on officials of the fourth rank and below.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month he was made imperial commissioner to suppress locusts in Henan, empowered to punish officials of the fourth rank and below.

sentences.zh: 宣宗憂旱。

translations.literal: Emperor Xuanzong was troubled by drought.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xuanzong brooded over the drought.

sentences.zh: 伯嘉奏曰：「日者君之象，陽之精，旱熯乃人君自用亢極之象，宰執以為冤獄所致。

translations.literal: Bojia memorialized: "The sun is the image of the ruler and the essence of yang; drought and scorching heat are signs of a ruler excessive self-will. The chancellors hold that wrongful imprisonments are the cause.
translations.idiomatic: Bojia wrote: "The sun is the emblem of the sovereign, the pure force of yang. Drought and blazing heat reflect a ruler who has pushed his will too far. Yet the chancellors blame it on unjust convictions in the courts.

sentences.zh: 夫燮和陰陽，宰相之職，而猥歸咎於有司。

translations.literal: Harmonizing yin and yang is the duty of the chancellor, yet they crudely shift the blame onto subordinate officials.
translations.idiomatic: To harmonize yin and yang is the chancellor office—but they shamelessly lay the fault on the clerks below them.

sentences.zh: 高琪武弁出身，固不足論，汝礪輩不知所職，其罪大矣。

translations.literal: Gao Qi rose from the ranks of military officers and is scarcely worth discussing; Ru Li and his like do not know their duties—their guilt is grave indeed.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Qi is a soldier by origin and hardly bears mention. But men like Ru Li do not even understand their own offices—that is a far graver failing.

sentences.zh: 漢制，災異策免三公，顧歸之有司邪。

translations.literal: Under the Han system, when calamities and portents occurred the Three Excellencies were dismissed by imperial rescript—yet are we to lay the blame on subordinate officials?
translations.idiomatic: Under Han law, when heaven sent omens, the Three Excellencies were removed by edict. Shall we now turn instead to scapegoating petty officials?

sentences.zh: 臣謂今日之旱，聖主自用，宰相諂諛，百司失職，實此之由。」

translations.literal: I hold that today drought stems from the sage ruler self-will, the chancellor flattery, and the hundred offices dereliction of duty—this is truly the cause.
translations.idiomatic: I say today drought comes of the Son of Heaven acting on his own impulse, of the chancellor sycophancy, and of the failure of the whole bureaucracy—that is the real source.

sentences.zh: 高琪、汝礪深怨之。

translations.literal: Gao Qi and Ru Li deeply resented this.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Qi and Ru Li nursed a deep hatred of him for it.

sentences.zh: 禮部郎中抹撚胡魯剌以言事忤旨，集五品以上官顯責之。

translations.literal: Mo Nian Hulu, a director in the Ministry of Rites, offended the emperor by speaking on state affairs; the emperor assembled officials of the fifth rank and above and publicly rebuked him.
translations.idiomatic: Mo Nian Hulu, a director in the Ministry of Rites, spoke on public affairs in a way that displeased the throne. The emperor gathered every official of the fifth rank and above and humiliated him before them all.

sentences.zh: 明日，伯嘉諫曰：「自古帝王莫不欲法堯、舜而恥為桀、紂，蓋堯、舜納諫，桀、紂拒諫也。

translations.literal: The next day Bojia remonstrated: "From antiquity, no emperor has failed to wish to model himself on Yao and Shun and to be ashamed of becoming Jie and Zhou—for Yao and Shun accepted remonstrance, while Jie and Zhou rejected it.
translations.idiomatic: The next day Bojia admonished the throne: "Every ruler in history has wanted to be like Yao and Shun and feared to be like Jie and Zhou. Yao and Shun welcomed counsel; Jie and Zhou turned it away.

sentences.zh: 故曰：'納諫者昌，拒諫者亡'。

translations.literal: Thus it is said: He who accepts remonstrance flourishes; he who rejects remonstrance perishes.
translations.idiomatic: Hence the saying: Accept remonstrance and prosper; reject remonstrance and fall.

sentences.zh: 胡魯剌所言是，無益於身，所言不是，無損于國。

translations.literal: If what Hulu spoke was right, it did him no personal benefit; if it was wrong, it did the state no harm.
translations.idiomatic: If Hulu was right, he gained nothing for himself. If he was wrong, the realm suffered no injury.

sentences.zh: 陛下廷辱如此，獨不欲為堯、舜乎？

translations.literal: Yet Your Majesty humiliates him thus in open court—do you truly not wish to be like Yao and Shun?
translations.idiomatic: Yet Your Majesty shames him like this in full audience—does the throne no longer aspire to Yao and Shun?

sentences.zh: 近日言事者語涉謗訕，有司當以重典，陛下釋之。

translations.literal: Recently those who spoke on affairs used language that touched on slander; the authorities would have applied the heavy statutes, yet Your Majesty released them.
translations.idiomatic: Lately, memorialists have used words that skirted sedition. The courts would have punished them under the severest law, but Your Majesty pardoned them.

sentences.zh: 與其釋之以為恩，曷若置之而不問。」

translations.literal: Better to have ignored the matter altogether than to pardon them and call it grace.
translations.idiomatic: It would have been better to say nothing at all than to release them and count it as a favor.

sentences.zh: 宰相請修山寨以避兵，伯嘉諫曰：「建議者必曰據險可以安君父，獨不見陳後主之入井乎？

translations.literal: When the chancellors proposed building mountain fortresses to escape the enemy, Bojia remonstrated: "Those who urge this will surely say that holding the high ground can keep the sovereign and his father safe—but have they never heard of how Chen Shubao went down the well?
translations.idiomatic: When the chancellors urged the building of mountain redoubts to flee the invaders, Bojia objected: "The advocates will say that secure heights can protect emperor and realm—but have they forgotten Chen Shubao hiding in his well?

sentences.zh: 假令入山寨可以得生，能複為國乎？

translations.literal: Even if retreating into mountain fortresses could preserve one life, could one afterward restore the state?
translations.idiomatic: Even if a mountain fortress could keep you alive, could you ever rebuild the kingdom from it?

sentences.zh: 人臣有忠國者，有媚君者，忠國者或拂君意，媚君者不為國謀。

translations.literal: Among ministers there are those loyal to the state and those who flatter the ruler; the loyal may go against the ruler wishes, while the flatterers do not plan for the state.
translations.idiomatic: Some ministers serve the country; others merely please their lord. The loyal may oppose the throne wishes; the flatterers never plan for the realm.

sentences.zh: 臣竊論之，有國可以有君，有君未必有國也。」

translations.literal: I venture to say: one may have a state and then have a ruler, but having a ruler does not necessarily mean one has a state.
translations.idiomatic: I would say this: a kingdom can exist before its king—but a king without a kingdom is no king at all.

sentences.zh: 高琪、汝礪聞之，怒愈甚。

translations.literal: When Gao Qi and Ru Li heard this, their anger grew all the greater.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Qi and Ru Li, hearing this, were more enraged than ever.

sentences.zh: 十二月，以御史中丞、權參知政事，元帥左監軍，行尚書省、元帥府于河中，控制河東南北路便宜從事。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, as Censor-in-Chief and acting Associate Administrator, left army supervisor of the commander-in-chief, he conducted the affairs of the Ministry Secretariat and the commander-in-chief headquarters at Hezhong, with discretionary authority over the northern and southern circuits of Hedong.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month he was named censor-in-chief and acting associate administrator, left army supervisor under the commander-in-chief, with the Secretariat and the marshal headquarters established at Hezhong and full discretionary power over the northern and southern routes of Hedong.

sentences.zh: 興定三年，伯嘉至河中，奏曰：「本路沖要，不可闕官，凡召辟者每以艱險為辭。

translations.literal: In the third year of Xingding, Bojia reached Hezhong and memorialized: "This circuit is strategically vital and cannot go without officials, yet those summoned or recruited often plead the hardships and dangers as an excuse.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Xingding, Bojia arrived in Hezhong and wrote: "This frontier is too critical to leave understaffed. Yet every man summoned to serve invents some excuse about hardship and danger.

sentences.zh: 乞凡檄召無故不至者宜令降罰，悉心幹當者視所曆升遷。」

translations.literal: I request that those summoned by edict who fail to come without good cause be demoted and penalized, while those who devote themselves wholeheartedly to their duties be promoted according to their record of service.
translations.idiomatic: I ask that anyone who ignores a summons without cause be demoted and punished, and that those who serve faithfully be promoted according to their merit.

sentences.zh: 詔召不至者決杖一百，餘如所請。

translations.literal: An edict ordered that those who failed to respond to summons be beaten one hundred strokes with the staff; the rest was granted as requested.
translations.idiomatic: The throne decreed one hundred strokes of the staff for anyone who failed to answer a summons; the remainder of his request was approved.

sentences.zh: 廷議欲棄河東，其民以實陝西。

translations.literal: At court there was discussion of abandoning Hedong and resettling its people in Shaanxi to strengthen that region.
translations.idiomatic: The court debated abandoning Hedong altogether and moving its population west into Shaanxi to fill out that province.

sentences.zh: 伯嘉上書諫曰：「中原之有河東，如人之有肩背。

translations.literal: Bojia submitted a remonstrance: "For the Central Plains to possess Hedong is like a man to possess shoulders and back.
translations.idiomatic: Bojia protested in a memorial: "Hedong to the heartland is what the shoulders and back are to a man.

sentences.zh: 古人雲'不得河東不雄'，萬一失之，恐未易取也。」

translations.literal: The ancients said, Without Hedong one cannot be mighty; if it were lost, I fear it would not be easily recovered.
translations.idiomatic: The ancients said: Without Hedong, no power endures. Lose it, and we may never win it back.

sentences.zh: 大忤宰執意。

translations.literal: This greatly offended the chancellors.
translations.idiomatic: This flew directly in the face of the chancellors plans.

sentences.zh: 頃之，召還，罷為中丞。

translations.literal: Before long he was recalled and demoted to Censor-in-Chief alone.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was recalled and stripped of his concurrent posts, retaining only the title of censor-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 伯嘉入見，奏曰：「如臣駑鈍，固宜召還，更須速遣大臣鎮撫。」

translations.literal: When Bojia had an audience, he memorialized: "One as dull and slow as myself ought indeed to be recalled; but a senior minister should be sent out at once to pacify and govern the region."
translations.idiomatic: On taking leave of the emperor, Bojia said: "A man as slow-witted as I am deserves to be recalled. But send a great minister at once to hold and settle the region."

sentences.zh: 宣宗深然之。

translations.literal: Emperor Xuanzong deeply agreed.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xuanzong agreed wholeheartedly.

sentences.zh: 伯嘉上疏曰：「國家兵不強，力不足以有為，財不富，賞不足以周眾，獨恃官爵以激勸人心。

translations.literal: Bojia submitted a memorial stating: "The state armies are not strong and its strength is insufficient for bold action; its wealth is not abundant and its rewards cannot reach everyone—it relies solely on rank and title to stir and encourage men hearts.
translations.idiomatic: Bojia wrote further: "Our armies are weak, our strength too small for great undertakings. Our treasury is thin, our rewards too few to go around. All we have left to move men hearts is rank and office.

sentences.zh: 近日以功遷官赴都求調者，有司往往駁之，冒濫者固十之三，既與而複奪之，非所以勸功也。

translations.literal: Recently those promoted for military merit who came to the capital seeking reassignment were often rejected by the authorities; though the unworthy may have been one in three, to grant promotion and then revoke it is no way to encourage merit.
translations.idiomatic: Lately, men promoted for battlefield merit have come to the capital seeking new appointments—and the ministries have turned many of them away. Perhaps a third were unworthy. But to grant a promotion and then snatch it back is no way to reward valor.

sentences.zh: 乞應軍功遷官，宣敕無偽者即准用之。」

translations.literal: I request that for promotions based on military merit, those whose imperial commissions are genuine be approved for appointment at once.
translations.idiomatic: I ask that any promotion earned in war, backed by a genuine imperial patent, be honored without delay.

sentences.zh: 又曰：「自兵興以來，河北桀黠往往聚眾自保，未有定屬。

translations.literal: He also said: "Since the outbreak of war, the cunning and fierce of Hebei have often gathered bands to protect themselves, and no fixed allegiance has been established.
translations.idiomatic: He added: "Since the wars began, the bold and unruly of Hebei have gathered in armed bands to protect themselves, and no one has yet brought them under the throne.

sentences.zh: 乞賜招撫，署以職名，無為他人所先。」

translations.literal: I request that they be granted recruitment and pacification, given official titles, lest others win them first.
translations.idiomatic: Offer them terms of surrender, give them offices, before some rival wins their loyalty first.

sentences.zh: 又曰：「河東、河北有能招集餘民完守城寨者，乞無問其門地，皆超逾等級，授以本處見任之職。」

translations.literal: He also said: "In Hedong and Hebei, those who can gather scattered people and restore and hold fortifications—I request that regardless of their family background, they all be promoted beyond their normal rank and given the highest local office available.
translations.idiomatic: He also wrote: "In Hedong and Hebei, any man who can rally survivors and hold a fortress—regardless of birth—should be raised above his station and given the highest post in his district.

sentences.zh: 又曰：「河中、晉安被山帶河，保障關、陝，此必爭之地。

translations.literal: He also said: "Hezhong and Jinan lie among mountains and rivers, guarding Tong Pass and Shaan—this is ground both sides must fight for.
translations.idiomatic: And again: "Hezhong and Jinan, ringed by mountains and rivers, guard the passes into Shaan—they are ground no enemy can afford to leave uncontested.

sentences.zh: 今雖殘破，形勢猶存，若使他人據之，因鹽池之饒，聚兵積糧，則河津以南，太行以西，皆不足恃矣。」

translations.literal: Though now ravaged and broken, the strategic position remains; if others occupy it, drawing on the wealth of the salt pools to gather troops and store grain, then south of the river crossings and west of the Taihang Mountains, nothing will be reliable.
translations.idiomatic: They are ruined now, but the terrain still matters. Let an enemy hold them, and with the riches of the salt pans to feed an army and fill granaries, everything south of the fords and west of the Taihang Range will lie open.

sentences.zh: 四年秋，河南大水，充宣慰副使，按行京東。

translations.literal: In the autumn of the fourth year, when Henan suffered great flooding, he was appointed deputy pacification commissioner and inspected Jingdong.
translations.idiomatic: In the autumn of the fourth year, after catastrophic floods in Henan, he was made deputy pacification commissioner and sent to inspect the eastern capital district.

sentences.zh: 奏曰：「亳州災最甚，合免三十余萬石。

translations.literal: He memorialized: "The disaster at Bozhou is the most severe; grain taxes there ought to be remitted by more than three hundred thousand shi.
translations.idiomatic: He reported: "Bozhou has suffered worst of all. More than three hundred thousand shi of grain should be forgiven there.

sentences.zh: 三司止奏除十萬石，民將重困，惟陛下憐之。」

translations.literal: The Three Departments have memorialized for remission of only one hundred thousand shi; the people will be sorely burdened again. I beg Your Majesty to show them compassion.
translations.idiomatic: The Three Departments ask to remit only one hundred thousand shi. The people will be crushed anew. I beg the throne to pity them.

sentences.zh: 詔治三司奏災不以實罪。

translations.literal: An edict ordered that the Three Departments be punished for reporting the disaster without full accuracy.
translations.idiomatic: An edict went out punishing the Three Departments for understating the scale of the disaster.

sentences.zh: 伯嘉行至蘄縣，聞前有紅襖賊，不敢至泗州。

translations.literal: When Bojia reached Qi County, he heard that Red Jacket bandits lay ahead and did not dare proceed to Sizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Bojia reached Qi County, learned that Red Jacket rebels blocked the road ahead, and did not dare continue on to Sizhou.

sentences.zh: 監察御史烏古孫奴申劾伯嘉違詔，不遍按視。

translations.literal: Supervising Censor Wugusun Nushen impeached Bojia for disobeying the edict and failing to conduct a full inspection.
translations.idiomatic: Supervising censor Wugusun Nushen impeached Bojia for defying his commission and failing to complete his tour of inspection.

sentences.zh: 又曰：「伯嘉知永城縣主簿蒙古訛裏刺不法，沈丘令夾谷陶也受賄，匿而不發。

translations.literal: He also said: "Bojia knew that Mengguo Elie, chief clerk of Yongcheng County, acted unlawfully, and that Jiahu Taoye, magistrate of Shenqiu, took bribes, yet concealed these facts and did not expose them.
translations.idiomatic: He added: "Bojia knew that Mengguo Elie, chief clerk of Yongcheng, broke the law, and that Jiahu Taoye, magistrate of Shenqiu, took bribes—yet he hid both crimes and filed no report.

sentences.zh: 前穀城縣令獨吉鼎術可嘗受業伯嘉，伯嘉諷御史辟之。」

translations.literal: The former magistrate of Gucheng, Duji Dingshu, had once studied under Bojia; Bojia hinted to the censors that he should be recruited.
translations.idiomatic: Duji Dingshu, former magistrate of Gucheng, had been Bojia student. Bojia quietly urged the censorate to appoint him.

sentences.zh: 詔有司鞫問，會赦免。

translations.literal: An edict ordered the authorities to investigate; an amnesty intervened and he was exempted.
translations.idiomatic: The throne ordered an inquiry, but a general amnesty came before judgment and he was cleared.

sentences.zh: 五年，起為彰化軍節度使，改翰林侍講學士。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he was reappointed military commissioner of Zhanghua Army and transferred to Hanlin Academician Reader-in-Waiting.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year he was restored as military commissioner of the Zhanghua army and made a Hanlin academician reader-in-waiting.

sentences.zh: 伯嘉純直，不能與時低昂，嘗曰：「生為男子，當益國澤民，其他不可學也。」

translations.literal: Bojia was upright and plainspoken and could not bend with the times. He once said: "Born a man, one ought to enrich the state and bring benefit to the people; nothing else is worth learning.
translations.idiomatic: Bojia was honest to a fault and would not trim his sails to the wind. He used to say: "A man is born to serve his country and his people. There is nothing else worth mastering.

sentences.zh: 高汝礪方希寵固位，伯嘉論事輒與之忤，由是毀之者眾。

translations.literal: Gao Ruli was then seeking favor to secure his position; whenever Bojia spoke on affairs he clashed with him, and for this reason those who slandered him were many.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Ruli was busy currying favor to keep his seat. Bojia contradicted him at every turn, and the men who worked to destroy Bojia reputation grew ever more numerous.

sentences.zh: 元光元年，坐言事過切，降遙授同知歸德府事。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yuanguang, for speaking too sharply on state affairs, he was demoted to honorary vice prefect of Guide Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Yuanguang, his memorials grew too cutting. He was demoted to honorary vice prefect of Guide.

sentences.zh: 二年三月，遙授集慶軍節度使，權參知政事，行尚書省於河中，率陝西精銳與平陽公史詠共複河東。

translations.literal: In the third month of the second year he was given the honorary post of military commissioner of Jiqing Army, acting Associate Administrator, conducting the Ministry Secretariat at Hezhong, leading the elite troops of Shaanxi together with the Prince of Pingyang, Shi Yong, to recover Hedong.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of the second year he was named honorary military commissioner of the Jiqing army, acting associate administrator, with the Secretariat at Hezhong. He led Shaanxi best troops alongside the Prince of Pingyang, Shi Yong, to retake Hedong.

sentences.zh: 頃之，伯嘉有疾。

translations.literal: Before long Bojia fell ill.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Bojia took sick.

sentences.zh: 六月，薨。

translations.literal: In the sixth month he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the sixth month.

sentences.zh: 伯嘉去太原後，完顏琢寓軍平定石仁寨，權平定州刺史范鐸以閻德用充本州提控。

translations.literal: After Bojia left Taiyuan, Wanyan Zhuo garrisoned his army at Shiren Fort in Pingding; Fan Duo, acting prefect of Pingding, appointed Yan Deyong as military controller of the prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: After Bojia departed Taiyuan, Wanyan Zhuo encamped at Shiren Fort in Pingding. Fan Duo, acting prefect of Pingding, named Yan Deyong military controller of the district.

sentences.zh: 德用桀驁，蓄奸謀，鐸不能制，委曲容庇之。

translations.literal: Deyong was fierce and arrogant and harbored treacherous designs; Duo could not control him and indulged him with evasions and shelter.
translations.idiomatic: Deyong was violent and scheming. Fan Duo could not restrain him and looked the other way.

sentences.zh: 興定元年，德用率所部掩襲，殺琢及官屬程珪等百餘人，遂據石仁寨。

translations.literal: In the first year of Xingding, Deyong led his troops in a surprise attack, killing Zhuo and more than a hundred officials including Cheng Gui, and then seized Shiren Fort.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Xingding, Deyong led his men in a night strike, slaughtered Zhuo and more than a hundred officials including Cheng Gui, and seized Shiren Fort.

sentences.zh: 鐸懼，挈家奔太原。

translations.literal: Duo was terrified, took his family, and fled to Taiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Terrified, Fan Duo gathered his family and fled to Taiyuan.

sentences.zh: 德用遂據平定州。

translations.literal: Deyong then occupied Pingding Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Deyong went on to take all of Pingding Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 二年十月，詔誅範鐸。

translations.literal: In the tenth month of the second year, an edict ordered Fan Duo executed.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month of the second year, an edict condemned Fan Duo to death.

sentences.zh: 朮虎筠壽

translations.literal: Zhuhu Yunshou
translations.idiomatic: Zhuhu Yunshou

sentences.zh: 朮虎筠壽，貞祐間為器物局直長，遷副使。

translations.literal: Zhuhu Yunshou, during the Zhenyou era, served as chief director of the Implements Bureau and was promoted to deputy commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: During the Zhenyou years, Zhuhu Yunshou served as chief director of the Implements Bureau and rose to deputy commissioner.

sentences.zh: 貞祐三年七月，工部下開封市白牯取皮治御用鞠仗。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of the third year of Zhenyou, the Ministry of Works ordered the opening of the Kaifeng market to buy white oxen and take their hides to make imperial ball-sticks.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of the third year of Zhenyou, the Ministry of Works ordered the Kaifeng market opened to purchase white oxen for their hides, to fashion new ball-sticks for the imperial court.

sentences.zh: 筠壽以其家所有鞠仗以進，因奏曰：「中都食盡，遠棄廟社，陛下當坐薪懸膽之日，奈何以球鞠細物動搖民間，使屠宰耕牛以供不急之用，非所以示百姓也。」

translations.literal: Yunshou presented ball-sticks from his own household and memorialized: "The central capital food is exhausted; we have abandoned the ancestral temples and altars. Your Majesty should be in the days of sitting upon firewood and hanging gall upon the wall—how can you, for the trivial matter of ball and stick, disturb the people, slaughtering plow oxen to supply an unurgent need? This is not how to show yourself to the common people."
translations.idiomatic: Yunshou offered ball-sticks from his own home and wrote: "The capital is starving. We have already forsaken the ancestral shrines. Your Majesty ought to be living as one who sleeps on brushwood and tastes gall every day—yet for the sake of a game of ball you would stir up the countryside, slaughtering draft oxen to satisfy a whim. This is no way to face the people."

sentences.zh: 宣宗不懌，擲仗籠中。

translations.literal: Emperor Xuanzong was displeased and threw the sticks back into their case.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xuanzong face darkened. He flung the sticks back into their cage.

sentences.zh: 明日，出筠壽為橋西提控。

translations.literal: The next day Yunshou was sent out as military controller west of the bridge.
translations.idiomatic: The next day Yunshou was posted out as military controller west of the bridge.

sentences.zh: 贊曰：孟鑄、宗端修、路鐸盡言于章宗，皆擯斥不遂。

translations.literal: The commentator says: Meng Zhu, Zong Duanxiu, and Lu Duo all spoke frankly to Emperor Zhangzong and were all driven out without achieving their aims.
translations.idiomatic: The historian comments: Meng Zhu, Zong Duanxiu, and Lu Duo all spoke their minds to Emperor Zhangzong—and all were cast aside, their counsel unheeded.

sentences.zh: 鑄劾胡沙虎，可謂先知，雖行其言，弗究厥罰。

translations.literal: When Zhu impeached Hushahu, he may be called prescient; though his words were acted upon, the full penalty was not pursued.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu denunciation of Hushahu showed true foresight. His warning was heeded in part, but the punishment never matched the crime.

sentences.zh: 厥後胡沙虎逆謀，胥持國終至於誤國，而不悟也。

translations.literal: Afterward Hushahu treacherous plot unfolded, and Xue Chiguo in the end brought ruin upon the state—yet still they did not awaken.
translations.idiomatic: Afterward Hushahu treason ran its course, and Xue Chiguo complacency finished the ruin of the realm—and still they would not see.

sentences.zh: 宣宗時，完顏素蘭、許古皆敢言者，亦挫于高琪、汝礪之手。

translations.literal: In Emperor Xuanzong time, Wanyan Sulan and Xu Gu were both men who dared to speak, yet they too were thwarted by Gao Qi and Ru Li.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Xuanzong, Wanyan Sulan and Xu Gu were men who spoke boldly—and they too were broken by Gao Qi and Ru Li.

sentences.zh: 匱土不能塞河決，有以也夫！

translations.literal: A basket of earth cannot stop a river from bursting its banks—there is reason in this!
translations.idiomatic: A basket of earth cannot hold back a river in flood. Small wonder, then!

sentences.zh: 完顏伯嘉以著功參大政，亦不能一朝而安，言之難也如是哉！

translations.literal: Wanyan Bojia, though distinguished in merit and participating in great affairs of state, could not find a single day peace either—such is the difficulty of speaking truth!
translations.idiomatic: Even Wanyan Bojia, a man of proven service who helped govern the realm, could not secure one tranquil day. To speak honestly in such times is harder still.

sentences.zh: 朮虎筠壽，所謂執藝事以諫者邪。

translations.literal: Zhuhu Yunshou—was he not what is meant by one who remonstrates through the office of his craft?
translations.idiomatic: Was Zhuhu Yunshou not precisely the sort of man who remonstrates through the duties of his own office?

sentences.zh: 張煒，字子明，洺州永年人，本名燝，避章宗嫌名改焉。

translations.literal: Zhang Wei, courtesy name Ziming, was a native of Yongnian in Mozhou. His original name was Jing; he changed it to avoid Zhangzong's taboo name.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Wei, styled Ziming, came from Yongnian in Mozhou. Born Jing, he changed his name to avoid Emperor Zhangzong's taboo.

sentences.zh: 大定二十五年進士，調葭州軍事判官，再遷中都左警巡使。

translations.literal: A jinshi of the twenty-fifth year of Dading, he was posted as military adjutant of Jia Prefecture, and was twice promoted to left patrol commissioner of the central capital.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination in the twenty-fifth year of Dading, served as military adjutant of Jia Prefecture, and was twice promoted, ending as left patrol commissioner of the central capital.

sentences.zh: 煒喜言功利，寡廉節，交通部民閻元翬，縉紳薄之。

translations.literal: Wei delighted in speaking of profit and utility, was deficient in integrity, associated with the local notable Yan Yuanhui of his native prefecture, and the gentry held him in contempt.
translations.idiomatic: Wei loved to talk profit and utility, cared little for integrity, kept company with a local notable of his home prefecture named Yan Yuanhui, and earned the contempt of the gentry.

sentences.zh: 累官部員外郎。

translations.literal: Through successive appointments he rose to vice director of the ministry.
translations.idiomatic: Through successive posts he rose to vice director of the ministry.

sentences.zh: 承安五年，天色久陰晦，平章政事張萬公奏：「此由君子小人邪正不分所致，君子宜在內，小人宜在外。」

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Chengan the sky remained overcast for a long time. Grand councilor Zhang Wangong memorialized: "This comes from failure to distinguish between the upright and the crooked, the gentleman and the petty man—the gentleman should be within, the petty man without."
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of Chengan the heavens stayed dark for many days. Grand councilor Zhang Wangong wrote: "This comes from failing to separate upright from crooked, gentleman from petty man. The gentleman belongs within; the petty man belongs without."

sentences.zh: 章宗問：「孰為小人？」

translations.literal: Emperor Zhangzong asked: "Who are the petty men?"
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Zhangzong asked, "Who are the petty men?"

sentences.zh: 萬公對曰：「戶部員外郎張煒、文繡署丞田櫟、都水監丞張嘉貞雖有幹才，無德而稱，好奔走以取勢利。

translations.literal: Wangong replied: "Vice Director of the Ministry of Revenue Zhang Wei, Embroidery Directorate Commissioner Tian Li, and Directorate of Waterways Vice Director Zhang Jiazhen, though possessed of practical talent, have no virtue to speak of and love to bustle about for power and profit.
translations.idiomatic: Wangong answered: "Vice director of the Ministry of Revenue Zhang Wei, embroidery directorate commissioner Tian Li, and waterways vice director Zhang Jiazhen have practical talent but no virtue worth the name, and love to scurry about for power and gain.

sentences.zh: 大抵論人當先德後才。」

translations.literal: In general, when judging men one should put virtue first and talent after."
translations.idiomatic: In judging men, virtue should come first and talent after."

sentences.zh: 詔三人皆與外除，煒出為同知鎮西軍節度使事，轉同知西京轉運使事。

translations.literal: An edict assigned all three to external posts. Wei was sent out as acting military commissioner of the Zhenxi army and then transferred to acting transport commissioner of the Western Capital.
translations.idiomatic: An edict posted all three outside the capital. Wei went out as acting military commissioner of the Zhenxi army, then became acting transport commissioner of the Western Capital.

sentences.zh: 是時，大築界牆，被行戶工部牒主役事。

translations.literal: At that time the border wall was being built on a large scale; he was conscripted as a requisitioned household, and the Ministry of Works issued a dispatch putting him in charge of corvée labor.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the border wall was being built on a vast scale. Wei was drafted as a requisitioned household, and the Ministry of Works dispatched him to oversee corvée labor.

sentences.zh: 丁母憂，起複桓州刺史，奏請以鹽易米事，且所言利害甚多，恐涉細碎，不敢盡上。

translations.literal: When his mother died he entered mourning, but was recalled to serve as prefect of Huanzhou. He memorialized on exchanging salt for grain, and because what he said of advantages and disadvantages was very extensive, fearing it might seem too minute in detail, he did not dare submit it all.
translations.idiomatic: After his mother's death he entered mourning, but was recalled from mourning to serve as prefect of Huanzhou. He memorialized on trading salt for grain; the points of advantage and disadvantage were so numerous that, fearing the matter too fine-grained, he did not dare submit all of it.

sentences.zh: 詔尚書省曰：「張煒通曉人也，朕不敢縷詰，卿等詳問之，毋為虛文。」

translations.literal: An edict to the Secretariat said: "Zhang Wei is a man of broad understanding. I dare not press him with minute questions. You should question him in detail and not treat this as empty formality."
translations.idiomatic: An edict to the Secretariat ran: "Zhang Wei is a man of real understanding. I will not press him with petty questions. Question him thoroughly yourselves, and do not reduce this to empty form."

sentences.zh: 充宣差西北路軍儲，自言斂不及民，可以足用。

translations.literal: He was appointed imperial commissioner for military stores on the Northwest Route, and declared of his own accord that he could levy without reaching the people and still make supplies sufficient.
translations.idiomatic: He was made imperial commissioner for Northwest Route military stores, and claimed that he could fill the need without levying on the people.

sentences.zh: 大抵募商賈縱其販易，不問所從來。

translations.literal: In general he recruited merchants, allowed them free trade, and did not ask whence goods came.
translations.idiomatic: Broadly speaking, he recruited merchants, let them trade freely, and never asked where their goods came from.

sentences.zh: 奸人往往投牒，妄指產業，疏鄰保姓名，煒信之，多與之錢。

translations.literal: Villains often submitted petitions, falsely claiming property and listing the names of neighbor-guarantors. Wei believed them and gave many of them money.
translations.idiomatic: Rascals often filed petitions falsely claiming property and naming neighbor-guarantors. Wei believed them and paid out large sums.

sentences.zh: 已而亡去，即逮系鄰保，使之代償，一路為之疲弊。

translations.literal: When the fraudsters had fled, he immediately seized and bound the neighbor-guarantors and made them pay compensation, and the whole route was worn down by it.
translations.idiomatic: Once the swindlers vanished, he seized the neighbor-guarantors and forced them to make restitution, until the entire route was exhausted by it.

sentences.zh: 以故舊氈罽繒絮皮革折給軍士，皆棄於道而去。

translations.literal: Old felt, woolens, silk floss, and leather given to soldiers in lieu of payment were all cast on the road and abandoned.
translations.idiomatic: Old felt, woolens, silk floss, and leather issued to soldiers in lieu of cash were thrown away along the roads.

sentences.zh: 歲餘，改戶部郎中，遷翰林直學士，俱兼規措職事。

translations.literal: After more than a year he was transferred to director of the Ministry of Revenue and promoted to Hanlin academician in attendance, both posts also carrying fiscal-planning duties.
translations.idiomatic: After a year and more he became director of the Ministry of Revenue and Hanlin academician in attendance, in both cases with fiscal-planning duties attached.

sentences.zh: 左丞相宗浩奏：「張煒長於恢辦，比戶部給錢三十萬，已增息十四萬矣。

translations.literal: Left chief councilor Zong Hao memorialized: "Zhang Wei excels at resource mobilization. Of the three hundred thousand cash the Ministry of Revenue gave him, he has already added one hundred and forty thousand in interest.
translations.idiomatic: Left chief councilor Zong Hao wrote: "Zhang Wei is skilled at resource mobilization. Of the three hundred thousand cash the Ministry of Revenue gave him, he has already turned a profit of one hundred and forty thousand.

sentences.zh: 請給錢通百萬，今從長恢辦，乞不隸省部，委臣專一提控，有應奏者，許煒專達，歲差幹事官計本息具奏。」

translations.literal: I request that the total grant be brought to one million cash, and that he now be allowed to mobilize resources on a larger scale. I beg that he not be subordinate to the ministries, but that I be entrusted to supervise him exclusively. When memorials are required, let Wei report directly. Each year dispatch an executive officer to calculate principal and interest and submit a full report."
translations.idiomatic: I ask that the grant be raised to one million cash and that he be allowed to mobilize resources on the largest scale. Let him no longer answer to the ministries; entrust exclusive supervision to me. When memorials are needed, let Wei report directly. Each year send an executive officer to reckon principal and interest and report in full."

sentences.zh: 上從其請。

translations.literal: The emperor granted the request.
translations.idiomatic: The throne approved.

sentences.zh: 泰和六年，伐宋，煒進銀五千兩。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Taihe, during the campaign against Song, Wei presented five thousand taels of silver.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year of Taihe, during the war against Song, Wei offered five thousand taels of silver.

sentences.zh: 詔曰：「汝幹集資儲，固其職也，毋令軍士有議國家。

translations.literal: An edict said: "You are diligent in gathering funds and stores—that is indeed your duty. Do not let soldiers speak ill of the state.
translations.idiomatic: An edict said: "To gather funds and stores is your proper work. Do not give soldiers cause to blame the state.

sentences.zh: 人之短汝，朕皆知之，惟能興利，斯惟汝功。」

translations.literal: What men say against you, I know it all. Only if you can create profit will that be your merit."
translations.idiomatic: I know every word spoken against you. If you can create profit, that alone will be your merit."

sentences.zh: 自西北路召還，勾計諸道倉庫，除簽三司事。

translations.literal: He was recalled from the Northwest Route, audited the granaries of all circuits, and was appointed co-signatory of the Three Commissions.
translations.idiomatic: Recalled from the Northwest Route, he audited the granaries of every circuit and was appointed co-signatory of the Three Commissions.

sentences.zh: 上問：「誰可代卿規措者？」

translations.literal: The emperor asked: "Who can replace you in fiscal planning?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor asked, "Who can take over your fiscal planning?"

sentences.zh: 煒舉中都轉運戶籍判官王謙。

translations.literal: Wei recommended Wang Qian, household-registration commissioner of the central capital transport office.
translations.idiomatic: Wei recommended Wang Qian, household-registration commissioner of the central capital transport office.

sentences.zh: 謙至西北路，盡發煒前後散失錢物以巨萬計，對獄者積年。

translations.literal: When Qian reached the Northwest Route, he fully exposed Wei's lost and misappropriated funds and goods, amounting to tens of thousands, and cases awaiting trial piled up for years.
translations.idiomatic: When Qian arrived on the Northwest Route, he uncovered Wei's missing and misappropriated funds and goods by the tens of thousands; trials backed up for years.

sentences.zh: 大安三年，起為同簽三司事。

translations.literal: In the third year of Da'an he was recalled to serve as co-signatory of the Three Commissions.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Da'an he was recalled to serve again as co-signatory of the Three Commissions.

sentences.zh: 會河堡兵敗，軍士猶去張宣差刻我，欲倒戈殺之。

translations.literal: When the Hebao garrison was defeated, the soldiers still resented Commissioner Zhang for gouging them and wanted to turn their spears and kill him.
translations.idiomatic: When the Hebao garrison was routed, the soldiers still burned with hatred of Commissioner Zhang for bleeding them dry and meant to turn their spears and kill him.

sentences.zh: 累遷戶部侍郎。

translations.literal: Through successive promotions he rose to vice minister of the Ministry of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: He rose by successive promotion to vice minister of the Ministry of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 貞祐初。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Zhenyou.
translations.idiomatic: At the opening of the Zhenyou era.

sentences.zh: 遷河北西路按察轉運使。

translations.literal: He was transferred to surveillance and transport commissioner of the Hebei West circuit.
translations.idiomatic: He was made surveillance and transport commissioner of the Hebei West circuit.

sentences.zh: 貞祐二年春，中都乏糧，詔同知都轉運使事。

translations.literal: In the spring of the second year of Zhenyou the central capital lacked grain, and he was ordered to serve as acting associate director of the metropolitan transport office.
translations.idiomatic: In spring of the second year of Zhenyou, with the capital short of grain, he was ordered to serve as acting associate director of the metropolitan transport office.

sentences.zh: 邊源以兵萬人護運通州積粟，軍敗死焉，平章政事高琪舉煒代源行六部事。

translations.literal: Bian Yuan, with ten thousand troops escorting stored grain from Tongzhou, was defeated and killed. Grand councilor Gao Qi recommended Wei to replace Yuan and conduct the affairs of the Six Ministries.
translations.idiomatic: Bian Yuan, commanding ten thousand men to escort stored grain from Tongzhou, was defeated and killed. Grand councilor Gao Qi recommended Wei to replace Yuan and handle the affairs of the Six Ministries.

sentences.zh: 以勞進官一階，改河北東路轉運使。

translations.literal: For his service he was promoted one rank and transferred to transport commissioner of the Hebei East circuit.
translations.idiomatic: For his labors he was promoted one rank and made transport commissioner of the Hebei East circuit.

sentences.zh: 宣宗遷汴，佐尚書右丞胥鼎前路排頓，及修南京宮闕。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xuanzong moved the court to Bian, he assisted Right Vice Director of the Secretariat Xu Ding in arranging the advance and in repairing the palace at the Southern Capital.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xuanzong moved the court to Bian, he assisted Right Vice Director Xu Ding in organizing the advance march and in repairing the Southern Capital palace.

sentences.zh: 無何，坐事降孟州防禦使。

translations.literal: Before long, for an offense he was demoted to defense commissioner of Meng Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Not long after, he was demoted to defense commissioner of Meng Prefecture for an offense.

sentences.zh: 三年，遷安國軍節度使。

translations.literal: In the third year he was transferred to military commissioner of the Anguo army.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year he was transferred to military commissioner of the Anguo army.

sentences.zh: 致仕。

translations.literal: He retired from office.
translations.idiomatic: He retired from office.

sentences.zh: 宣宗初以煒有才，既察其無實，遂不复用。

translations.literal: At first Emperor Xuanzong thought Wei had talent, but once he saw that he lacked substance, he never employed him again.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xuanzong had first thought Wei talented, but once he saw there was nothing solid in him, he never used him again.

sentences.zh: 貞祐四年卒。

translations.literal: He died in the fourth year of Zhenyou.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the fourth year of Zhenyou.

sentences.zh: 高竑，渤海人。

translations.literal: Gao Hong was a man of Bohai.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Hong came from Bohai.

sentences.zh: 以廕補官，累調貴德縣尉。

translations.literal: He entered office by hereditary privilege and through successive assignments rose to county captain of Guide.
translations.idiomatic: He entered service by yin privilege and through successive posts rose to county captain of Guide.

sentences.zh: 提刑司舉任繁劇，遷奉聖州錄事。

translations.literal: The Chief Punishments Office recommended him for heavy and demanding duties, and he was transferred to registrar of Fengsheng Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: The Chief Punishments Office recommended him for arduous duty, and he was transferred to registrar of Fengsheng Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 察廉，遷內黃令，累官左藏庫副使。

translations.literal: After an integrity inspection he was transferred to magistrate of Neihuang and through successive posts rose to deputy director of the Left Treasury.
translations.idiomatic: Passed in an integrity review, he became magistrate of Neihuang and eventually rose to deputy director of the Left Treasury.

sentences.zh: 元妃李氏以皁弊易紅幣，竑獨拒不肯易。

translations.literal: Primary consort Lady Li of the Yuan consort clan wished to exchange worn black coins for red coins, but Hong alone refused and would not exchange them.
translations.idiomatic: Primary consort Lady Li of the Yuan consort clan wanted to swap worn black coins for red coins, but Hong alone refused the exchange.

sentences.zh: 元妃奏之。

translations.literal: The primary consort reported it.
translations.idiomatic: The primary consort reported the matter.

sentences.zh: 章宗大喜，遣人諭之曰：「所執甚善。

translations.literal: Emperor Zhangzong was greatly pleased and sent someone to instruct him: "What you upheld was very good.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Zhangzong was greatly pleased and sent word: "You did well to hold the line.

sentences.zh: 今姑與之，後不得為例。」

translations.literal: For now let her have the exchange, but afterward this must not be made a precedent."
translations.idiomatic: Let her have it this once, but it must not become a precedent."

sentences.zh: 轉儀鸞局、少府少監，改戶部員外郎、安州刺史。

translations.literal: He was transferred to the Ceremonial Carriages Bureau and vice director of the Palace Manufactories, then changed to vice director of the Ministry of Revenue and prefect of An Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to the Ceremonial Carriages Bureau and vice director of the Palace Manufactories, then made vice director of the Ministry of Revenue and prefect of An Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 大安中，越王永功判中山，竑以王傅同知府事。

translations.literal: In the Da'an era Prince Yonggong of Yue held authority at Zhongshan, and Hong served as tutor to the prince and jointly managed prefectural affairs.
translations.idiomatic: During the Da'an years Prince Yonggong of Yue governed Zhongshan, and Hong served as his tutor while jointly managing prefectural affairs.

sentences.zh: 改同知河南府，充安撫使。

translations.literal: He was changed to acting prefect of Henan Prefecture and appointed pacification commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: He was made acting prefect of Henan Prefecture and appointed pacification commissioner.

sentences.zh: 徙同知大名府，兼本路安撫使。

translations.literal: He was transferred to acting prefect of Daming Prefecture, also serving as pacification commissioner of that circuit.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to acting prefect of Daming Prefecture, concurrently pacification commissioner of that circuit.

sentences.zh: 貞祐二年，遷河北西路按察轉運使，錄大名功，遷三官，致仕。

translations.literal: In the second year of Zhenyou he was transferred to surveillance and transport commissioner of the Hebei West circuit. His service at Daming was recorded as merit, he was promoted three ranks, and he retired from office.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Zhenyou he became surveillance and transport commissioner of the Hebei West circuit. His achievements at Daming were entered as merit, he was promoted three ranks, and he retired.

sentences.zh: 興定四年，卒。

translations.literal: He died in the fourth year of Xingding.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the fourth year of Xingding.

sentences.zh: 李複亨

translations.literal: Li Fuheng
translations.idiomatic: Li Fuheng

sentences.zh: 李複亨，字仲修，榮州河津人。

translations.literal: Li Fuheng, courtesy name Zhongxiu, was a native of Hejin in Rong Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Li Fuheng, styled Zhongxiu, came from Hejin in Rong Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 年十八，登進士第。

translations.literal: At eighteen he passed the jinshi examination.
translations.idiomatic: At eighteen he passed the jinshi examination.

sentences.zh: 複中書判優等，調臨晉主簿。

translations.literal: He again placed in the superior grade on the Secretariat examination and was posted as chief clerk of Linjin.
translations.idiomatic: He placed in the superior grade on the Secretariat examination and was posted as chief clerk of Linjin.

sentences.zh: 護送官馬入府，宿逆旅，有盜殺馬，複亨曰：「不利而殺之，必有仇者。」

translations.literal: While escorting official horses to the prefecture he lodged at an inn, and a thief killed a horse. Fuheng said: "To kill it without taking it shows there must be someone with a grudge."
translations.idiomatic: While escorting official horses to the prefecture he lodged at an inn, where a thief killed a horse. Fuheng said, "To kill it without stealing it means there must be a personal enemy."

sentences.zh: 盡索逆旅商人過客。

translations.literal: He had all the merchants and travelers at the inn searched.
translations.idiomatic: He had every merchant and traveler at the inn searched.

sentences.zh: 同邑人橐中盛佩刀，謂之曰：「刀蔑馬血，火煆之則刃青。」

translations.literal: A man from his home county had a sheathed knife in his bag. Fuheng said to him: "If the knife wiped horse blood and is fired in flame, the blade will turn blue."
translations.idiomatic: A man from his home county carried a sheathed knife in his bag. Fuheng told him, "Smear the blade with the horse's blood and heat it in fire—the steel will turn blue."

sentences.zh: 其人款服，果有仇。

translations.literal: The man confessed fully; there was indeed a grudge.
translations.idiomatic: The man confessed; there had indeed been a grudge.

sentences.zh: 以提刑薦遷南和令。

translations.literal: On recommendation from the Chief Punishments Office he was transferred to magistrate of Nanhe.
translations.idiomatic: Recommended by the Chief Punishments Office, he was made magistrate of Nanhe.

sentences.zh: 盜割民家牛耳。

translations.literal: Someone stole and cut off a farmer's ox ear.
translations.idiomatic: Someone stole into a farmer's house and cut off an ox's ear.

sentences.zh: 複亨盡召裏中人至，使牛家牽牛遍過之，至一人前，牛忽驚躍，詰之，乃引伏。

translations.literal: Fuheng summoned everyone in the village, had the ox's owner lead the ox past them one by one, and before one man the ox suddenly started and leapt. When questioned, the man confessed.
translations.idiomatic: Fuheng summoned everyone in the village, had the owner lead the ox past them one by one, and when the beast suddenly shied and leapt before one man, questioning brought a confession.

sentences.zh: 察廉，遷臨洮府判官，改陝西東路戶籍判官，轉河東北路支度判官。

translations.literal: After an integrity inspection he was transferred to adjutant of Lintao Prefecture, changed to household-registration commissioner of the Shaanxi East circuit, and transferred to expenditure commissioner of the Hedong North circuit.
translations.idiomatic: Passed in an integrity review, he became adjutant of Lintao Prefecture, then household-registration commissioner of the Shaanxi East circuit, and then expenditure commissioner of the Hedong North circuit.

sentences.zh: 泰和中，伐宋，充宣撫司經歷官，遷解鹽副使，曆保大、震武同知節度事。

translations.literal: In the Taihe era, during the campaign against Song, he served as administrative aide on the pacification staff, was transferred to deputy salt commissioner of Jie, and successively held acting military commissioner posts at Baoda and Zhenwu.
translations.idiomatic: During the Taihe campaign against Song he served on the pacification staff, became deputy salt commissioner of Jie, and held acting military commissioner posts at Baoda and Zhenwu in turn.

sentences.zh: 丁母憂，起複同知震武節度，加遙授忻州刺史。

translations.literal: When his mother died he entered mourning, but was recalled to serve as acting military commissioner of Zhenwu and was additionally given the honorary title of prefect of Xin Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: After his mother's death he entered mourning, but was recalled to serve as acting military commissioner of Zhenwu and given the honorary title of prefect of Xin Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 貞祐間，曆左司員外郎、郎中，遷翰林直學士行三司事。

translations.literal: During Zhenyou he successively served as vice director and director in the Left Secretariat and was promoted to Hanlin academician in attendance acting as head of the Three Commissions.
translations.idiomatic: During Zhenyou he rose through vice director and director in the Left Secretariat, then became Hanlin academician in attendance acting as head of the Three Commissions.

sentences.zh: 興定三年，上言：「近日興師伐宋，恐宋人乘虛掩襲南鄙，故籍邊郡民為軍。

translations.literal: In the third year of Xingding he memorialized: "Recently troops were raised to campaign against Song, for fear Song might seize the opportunity to raid the southern frontier, so border commandery people were registered as soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Xingding he memorialized: "Troops were recently raised to campaign against Song, and fearing a Song raid on the southern frontier, people of the border commanderies were registered as soldiers.

sentences.zh: 今大軍已還，乞罷遣歸本業。」

translations.literal: Now that the main army has returned, I beg that they be dismissed and sent back to their original occupations."
translations.idiomatic: Now that the main army has returned, I ask that they be dismissed and sent back to their original occupations."

sentences.zh: 從之。

translations.literal: The request was granted.
translations.idiomatic: The throne agreed.

sentences.zh: 複亨舉陳留縣令程震等二十九人農桑有效，征科均一，朝廷皆遷擢之。

translations.literal: Fuheng recommended twenty-nine men, including Chenliu magistrate Cheng Zhen, for effective farming and sericulture and even tax collection; the court promoted them all.
translations.idiomatic: Fuheng recommended twenty-nine officials, including Chenliu magistrate Cheng Zhen, for effective farming and sericulture and even tax collection, and the court promoted them all.

sentences.zh: 是歲七月，置京東、京西、京南三路行三司，掌勸農催租、軍須科差及鹽鐵酒榷等事，戶部侍郎張師魯攝東路，治歸德，戶部侍郎完顏麻斤出攝南路，治許州，複亨攝西路，治中京實河南府，三司使侯摯總之。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of that year traveling Three Commissions offices were established for the East Capital, West Capital, and South Capital routes, charged with encouraging agriculture, collecting rent, military requisitions and corvée, and salt, iron, and wine monopolies. Vice Minister of Revenue Zhang Shilu acted for the East Route with seat at Guide; Vice Minister of Revenue Wanyan Majin went out to act for the South Route with seat at Xuzhou; Fuheng acted for the West Route with seat at the Central Capital, in practice Henan Prefecture; Commissioner of the Three Commissions Hou Zhi had overall charge.
translations.idiomatic: That seventh month saw traveling Three Commissions established for the East, West, and South Capital routes, overseeing farming, rent collection, military supplies, corvée, and the salt, iron, and wine monopolies. Vice minister Zhang Shilu acted for the East Route from Guide; vice minister Wanyan Majin went out to act for the South Route from Xuzhou; Fuheng acted for the West Route from the Central Capital—that is, Henan Prefecture—under Three Commissions commissioner Hou Zhi.

sentences.zh: 複亨奏：「民間銷毀農具以供軍器，臣竊以為未便。

translations.literal: Fuheng memorialized: "The people are melting down farm tools to supply military equipment. I privately think this inexpedient.
translations.idiomatic: Fuheng wrote: "The people are melting down farm tools for military equipment. I do not think this wise.

sentences.zh: 汝州魯山、寶豐，鄧州南陽皆產鐵，募工置冶，可以獲利，且不厲民。」

translations.literal: Lushan and Baofeng in Ru Prefecture and Nanyang in Deng Prefecture all produce iron. If workers are recruited and smelting works established, profit can be gained without harrying the people.
translations.idiomatic: Lushan and Baofeng in Ru Prefecture and Nanyang in Deng Prefecture all have iron. Recruit workers and set up smelters, and profit can be gained without harrying the people."

sentences.zh: 又奏：「陽武設賣鹽官以佐軍用，乞禁止滄，濱鹽勿令過河，河南食陽武、解鹽，河北食滄、濱鹽，南北俱濟。」

translations.literal: He also memorialized: "Yangwu has established salt-selling offices to assist military expenses. I beg that Cang and Bin salt be forbidden to cross the river: Henan should consume Yangwu and Jie salt, Hebei should consume Cang and Bin salt, so that north and south are both provided for."
translations.idiomatic: He also wrote: "Yangwu has set up salt-selling offices to support the army. Forbid Cang and Bin salt to cross the river: let Henan eat Yangwu and Jie salt, and Hebei eat Cang and Bin salt, so both north and south are supplied.

sentences.zh: 詔尚書省行之。

translations.literal: An edict ordered the Secretariat to carry it out.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered the Secretariat to implement it.

sentences.zh: 九月，以勸農有勞，遷兵部尚書。

translations.literal: In the ninth month, for labor in encouraging agriculture, he was transferred to minister of the Ministry of War.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month, for his work encouraging agriculture, he was made minister of war.

sentences.zh: 再閱月，轉吏部尚書，權參知政事。

translations.literal: After another month he was transferred to minister of the Ministry of Personnel and given acting status as participation councillor.
translations.idiomatic: A month later he became minister of personnel and acting participation councillor.

sentences.zh: 四年三月，真拜參知政事，兼修國史。

translations.literal: In the third month of the fourth year he was formally appointed participation councillor and also charged with compiling the national history.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of the fourth year he was formally appointed participation councillor and charged with compiling the national history.

sentences.zh: 七月，河南雨水害稼，複亨為宣慰使，御史中丞完顏伯嘉副之，循行郡縣，凡官吏貪污不治者，得廢罷推治。

translations.literal: In the seventh month rain in Henan damaged the crops. Fuheng was made pacification commissioner, with censor-in-chief Wanyan Bojia as his deputy. They toured the commanderies and counties, and wherever officials were corrupt or failed to govern, they could dismiss them and push for prosecution.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month flooding in Henan ruined the crops. Fuheng was made pacification commissioner, with censor-in-chief Wanyan Bojia as deputy. Touring commanderies and counties, they could dismiss corrupt or negligent officials and push for prosecution.

sentences.zh: 複亨奏乞禁宣慰司官吏不得與州府司縣行總管府及管軍官會飲。

translations.literal: Fuheng memorialized requesting a ban on pacification staff dining together with prefectural, county, circuit chief, and military command officials.
translations.idiomatic: Fuheng asked that pacification staff be forbidden to feast with prefectural, county, circuit chief, and military command officials.

sentences.zh: 又奏曰：「詔書令臣，民間差發可免者免之。

translations.literal: He also memorialized: "The edict orders me that among corvée levies on the people, whatever can be exempted should be exempted.
translations.idiomatic: He also wrote: "The edict instructs me that among corvée levies on the people, whatever can be remitted should be remitted.

sentences.zh: 民養驛馬，此役最甚，使者求索百端，皆出養馬之家，人多逃竄，職此之由。

translations.literal: The people maintain relay horses; this corvée is the heaviest. Envoys demand in every possible way, and all costs fall on horse-keeping households, so many people flee and hide—this is the reason.
translations.idiomatic: Maintaining relay horses is the heaviest burden. Envoys demand endlessly, and every cost falls on the horse-keeping households; that is why so many flee.

sentences.zh: 可依舊設回馬官，使者食料皆官給之，歲終會計，均賦於民。」

translations.literal: The old system of relay-horse officers may be restored; envoys' provisions should all be supplied by the state, and at year's end accounts should be settled and the cost evenly assessed on the people.
translations.idiomatic: Restore the old relay-horse officers. Let the state supply envoys' provisions, settle accounts at year's end, and spread the cost evenly among the people.

sentences.zh: 又奏：「河南閒田多，可招河東、河北移民耕種。

translations.literal: He also memorialized: "There is much idle land in Henan; immigrants from Hedong and Hebei can be recruited to cultivate it.
translations.idiomatic: He also wrote: "Henan has much idle land. Recruit settlers from Hedong and Hebei to farm it.

sentences.zh: 被災及沿邊郡縣租稅全免，內地半之，以救塗炭之民，資蓄積之用。」

translations.literal: In disaster-struck and border commanderies and counties rent and tax should be wholly remitted; in the interior, half—so as to rescue people in utter misery and build up stores.
translations.idiomatic: In stricken and border counties remit rent and tax entirely; in the interior, half—both to rescue people in misery and to build up reserves.

sentences.zh: 詔有司議行焉。

translations.literal: An edict ordered the responsible offices to discuss implementation.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered the responsible offices to discuss implementation.

sentences.zh: 還奏：「南陽禾麥雖傷，土性宜稻，今因久雨，乃更滋茂。

translations.literal: On his return he memorialized: "Though grain and wheat at Nanyang were damaged, the soil suits rice, and now because of the long rains it has grown all the more luxuriant.
translations.idiomatic: On returning he reported: "Though grain and wheat at Nanyang were harmed, the soil suits rice, and the long rains have made it grow all the more lush.

sentences.zh: 田凡五百餘頃，畝可收五石，都得二十五萬余石。

translations.literal: The fields total more than five hundred qing; each mu can yield five shi, altogether more than two hundred and fifty thousand shi.
translations.idiomatic: The fields total more than five hundred qing; each mu can yield five shi, for more than two hundred and fifty thousand shi in all.

sentences.zh: 可增直糴稻給唐、鄧軍食。

translations.literal: Rice can be purchased at a premium to supply the armies at Tang and Deng.
translations.idiomatic: Rice can be bought at premium price to feed the armies at Tang and Deng.

sentences.zh: 緣詔書不急科役即令免罷，臣不敢輒行，如以臣言為然，乞付有司計之。」

translations.literal: Because the edict says that non-urgent corvée should immediately be exempted and stopped, I do not dare act on my own. If my words are deemed sound, I beg that this be referred to the responsible offices for calculation.
translations.idiomatic: Because the edict says non-urgent corvée must at once be exempted and halted, I dare not act on my own. If my proposal is sound, I ask that the responsible offices be ordered to calculate it.

sentences.zh: 制可。

translations.literal: The edict approved.
translations.idiomatic: Approval was granted.

sentences.zh: 無何，被詔提控軍興糧草。

translations.literal: Before long he was ordered by edict to take charge of fodder and grain for the war effort.
translations.idiomatic: Before long an edict put him in charge of fodder and grain for the war effort.

sentences.zh: 複亨奏：「河渡不通，陝西鹽價踴貴，乞以粟互易足兵食。」

translations.literal: Fuheng memorialized: "River crossings are blocked and salt prices in Shaanxi have soared. I beg that grain be exchanged for salt to make army rations sufficient.
translations.idiomatic: Fuheng wrote: "River crossings are blocked and Shaanxi salt prices have soared. I ask that grain be traded for salt to fill army rations.

sentences.zh: 詔戶部從長規措。

translations.literal: An edict ordered the Ministry of Revenue to plan as best it could.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered the Ministry of Revenue to arrange matters as best it could.

sentences.zh: 複亨有會計才，號能吏，當時推服，故驟至通顯。

translations.literal: Fuheng had talent for accounts and was known as a capable official; his contemporaries admired him, and therefore he rose swiftly to high prominence.
translations.idiomatic: Fuheng had a gift for accounts and was known as a capable official; contemporaries respected him, and he rose swiftly to high office.

sentences.zh: 既執政，頗矜持，以私自營，譽望頓減。

translations.literal: Once in government he was rather self-important and pursued private gain, and his reputation suddenly declined.
translations.idiomatic: Once in power he grew self-important and pursued private gain, and his reputation collapsed.

sentences.zh: 五年三月，廷試進士，複亨監試。

translations.literal: In the third month of the fifth year the palace examination for jinshi was held, and Fuheng supervised the examination.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of the fifth year Fuheng supervised the palace examination for jinshi.

sentences.zh: 進士盧元謬誤，濫放及第。

translations.literal: The jinshi Lu Yuan was in error, yet was indiscriminately passed and granted the degree.
translations.idiomatic: The candidate Lu Yuan was unqualified, yet was passed and granted the degree anyway.

sentences.zh: 讀卷官禮部尚書趙秉文、翰林待制崔禧、歸德治中時戩、應奉翰林文字程嘉善當奪三官降職，複亨當奪兩官。

translations.literal: The examiners—Minister of Rites Zhao Bingwen, Hanlin Attendant-in-Waiting Cui Xi, Guide Administrative Director Shi Ji, and Hanlin Attendant Cheng Jiashan—should each have three ranks stripped and be demoted; Fuheng should have two ranks stripped.
translations.idiomatic: The examiners—minister of rites Zhao Bingwen, Hanlin attendant Cui Xi, Guide administrative director Shi Ji, and Hanlin attendant Cheng Jiashan—were each to lose three ranks and be demoted; Fuheng was to lose two.

sentences.zh: 趙秉文嘗請致仕，宣宗憐其老，降兩階，以禮部尚書致仕。

translations.literal: Zhao Bingwen had once requested retirement; Emperor Xuanzong pitied his age, reduced him two ranks, and let him retire as Minister of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Bingwen had once asked to retire; Emperor Xuanzong pitied his age, reduced him two ranks, and let him retire as minister of rites.

sentences.zh: 複亨罷為定國軍節度使。

translations.literal: Fuheng was dismissed and made military commissioner of the Dingguo army.
translations.idiomatic: Fuheng was dismissed and sent out as military commissioner of the Dingguo army.

sentences.zh: 元光元年十一月，城破自殺，年四十六。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month of the first year of Yuanguang, when the city fell he killed himself, aged forty-six.
translations.idiomatic: When the city fell in the eleventh month of the first year of Yuanguang, he took his own life at forty-six.

sentences.zh: 贈資德大夫、知河中府事。

translations.literal: He was posthumously granted Grand Master of Virtuous Talent and administrator of Hezhong prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously granted the title Grand Master of Virtuous Talent and named administrator of Hezhong.

sentences.zh: 贊曰：大凡兵興則財用不足，是故張煒、李複亨乘時射利，聚斂為功。

translations.literal: The commentator says: In general when war arises finances are insufficient; therefore Zhang Wei and Li Fuheng seized the moment to pursue profit and made extortion their achievement.
translations.idiomatic: The historian comments: When war breaks out, revenue always falls short—so Zhang Wei and Li Fuheng seized the moment for profit and made extortion their path to merit.

sentences.zh: 大安，軍士欲倒戈殺煒。

translations.literal: In Da'an the soldiers wanted to turn their spears and kill Wei.
translations.idiomatic: In Da'an the soldiers meant to turn their spears on Wei and kill him.

sentences.zh: 複亨宣慰南陽，還奏稻熟可糴。

translations.literal: Fuheng pacified Nanyang and on his return memorialized that the rice was ripe and could be purchased.
translations.idiomatic: Fuheng toured Nanyang as pacification commissioner and reported on his return that the rice crop was ripe and ready for purchase.

sentences.zh: 所謂聚斂之臣者，二子之謂矣。

translations.literal: What is meant by ministers who extort and gather wealth—these two men are the reference.
translations.idiomatic: These two were precisely what is meant by ministers who enrich themselves at the people's expense.

sentences.zh: 高竑之守藏，君子頗有取焉。

translations.literal: Gao Hong's guarding of the treasury—gentlemen found much in it to approve.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Hong's steadfast guarding of the treasury won considerable approval among gentlemen.
